jobs.description:
Another Source's client, OHSU Foundation
, is recruiting a Managing Director of Finance
to join their team in Portland, Oregon.

Here's a little about OHSU Foundation:

OHSU Foundation exists to advance the mission of Oregon Health & Science University by connecting the generosity of donors with opportunities to transform health, education, and discovery. Its financial enterprise reflects both the scale and complexity of that mission: the Foundation oversees financial activity and reporting for more than $2 billion in invested assets
, including more than 1,000 endowments, 40 trusts, and 150 annuities
.

Working at the intersection of philanthropy, healthcare, higher education, and finance, the Foundation partners closely with OHSU leaders, faculty, donors, trustees, and external advisors to ensure philanthropic resources are managed responsibly and positioned for long-term impact.

About this role:

The Managing Director of Finance is a senior financial leadership opportunity with broad influence across OHSU Foundation. Reporting to the CFO – VP of Finance & Administration, this leader will help shape and implement financial strategy while overseeing critical areas including financial reporting, fund and endowment accounting, trust administration, internal controls, audit, and financial policy.

Just as importantly, this is a highly collaborative role. You will serve as a strategic advisor to Foundation leadership, the Board of Trustees and its committees, and OHSU finance and faculty partners—translating complex financial information into insights that support decision-making, donor stewardship, and the effective use of philanthropic funds.

Scope & Impact

Financial Reporting, Ledgers & Donor Fund Accounts – 40%:
Lead financial reporting and accounting activities while ensuring compliance with appropriate GASB and regulatory requirements.
Develop meaningful financial and operational information that gives Foundation leadership actionable insights and supports sound decision-making.
Lead monthly and annual close processes and coordinate financial consolidation activities with OHSU.
Co-lead the annual audit, partnering with the external audit team and OHSU financial partners to establish timelines, resolve issues, and successfully complete the process.
Design, implement, and monitor internal controls over financial reporting while protecting the integrity of the Foundation's financial reporting systems.
Evaluate and evolve accounting and reporting practices as contributions, funds under management, regulatory requirements, and gift complexity continue to grow.
Partner with key OHSU faculty and finance leaders to provide strategic financial guidance and support the effective use of Foundation gift funds.
Trust Administration & Endowment Accounting – 30%:
Develop and implement approaches to assess and manage risk associated with charitable gift annuity agreements and provide regular updates to the Investment Committee.
Collaborate with gift planning colleagues to optimize trust and annuity administration.
Donor Strategy & Stewardship – 20%:
Partner with Foundation and OHSU stakeholders to inform strategies for top donor relationships and strengthen financial stewardship.
Develop sophisticated financial reporting and analysis to turn complex data into useful insights for strategic partners.
Leadership, Management & Department Operations – 10%:
Lead, coach, mentor, and evaluate Finance and Accounting staff while building the team's capabilities and ensuring critical responsibilities are effectively cross-trained.
Develop and maintain accounting and finance policies and procedures and serve as a trusted resource on complex financial matters.
Evaluate unusual assets and complex gift scenarios and provide thoughtful financial recommendations.
Help translate Board-approved financial and investment policy into effective operating practices across the organization.

Qualifications

Master's degree in accounting, finance, business administration, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
10+ years of broad experience across investment, tax, and general accounting.
Demonstrated expertise in generally accepted accounting principles, nonprofit accounting, investment and endowment accounting, tax reporting, and financial reporting systems.
Strong understanding of investment concepts, practices, and procedures.
Experience managing and assessing financial and business risk and developing appropriate recommendations.
Exceptional analytical skills, including the ability to locate, model, interpret, and communicate complex financial information from multiple sources.
Advanced capability with financial reporting, large data sets, accounting systems, Microsoft Office, and database applications.
Proven leadership experience, including successfully managing, mentoring, developing, retaining, and recruiting professional staff.
Ability to effectively advise and collaborate with senior leadership, staff, trustees, faculty partners, and external constituents.
Strong communication and influencing skills with the ability to make complex financial concepts accessible to varied audiences.
Demonstrated accountability, sound judgment, and ownership of programs, projects, and outcomes.
CPA certification preferred.

What's in it for you:

The anticipated annual salary range for this position is $126,000–$168,000
.
OHSU Foundation is open to a flexible hybrid work arrangement based on the needs of the role and team.

Beyond compensation, this role offers the opportunity to lead finance at significant scale and complexity while supporting a philanthropic organization closely connected to OHSU's work in healthcare, research, and education. The Office of University Development maximizes private support for the University of Michigan.

Job Summary

You will direct the major gift program and represent the breadth of the University of Michigan in that region. You will develop short- and long-term strategies to secure major and planned gifts ($100,000 or more) in collaboration with senior academic leaders and development colleagues within a decentralized development environment. Your primary responsibilities will be met through regular visits to U-M constituents within your assigned region. You will focus on 'fieldwork' with established donors and on discovering new prospective donors. This role requires regular travel and participation in evening and weekend activities.

Reports to:
Senior Director of Major Gifts, Midwestern States

Supervises:
Functional Supervision of Shared Project and Administrative Coordinator

Responsibilities*

Direct Fundraising (70%)

Identify, qualify, cultivate, solicit, and steward major and planned gift prospects through thoughtful, deliberate strategies, producing a stream of donors who can make gifts of $100,000 or more throughout the region.
Manage a portfolio of ~60-80 major gift prospects with emphasis to those prospects who require a university-wide lens (multiple degrees, demonstrated interest in multiple schools or programs).
Provide leadership for the region's major and planned gift activities by focusing on prospects under personal management and supporting solicitations directed by other staff. Ensure that major gift prospects are cultivated and solicited deliberately.
Keep a pace of discovery work throughout the region.
Maintain a pace of 120+ visits, 15+ asks, and 10+ closed gifts per year.

Strategic Leadership and SCCU Collaboration (20%)

Work with our Senior Director of Major Gifts, Midwestern States to plan and lead a regional fundraising strategy that supports prospect/donor identification, engagement, solicitation, and stewardship.
Plan and execute events that directly support regional goals.
Develop collaborative, productive relationships with our SCCU colleagues.
Advise our senior campus leadership (deans, directors, executive officers) on donor strategy and trip planning.
Attend quarterly retreats with our National Major Gifts Team and retreats with the Major Gifts Programs in the Office of University Development.

Volunteer Management (10%)

Recruit and sustain a volunteer network and committee structure in the region to multiply efforts in prospect identification, cultivation, and solicitation.
Provide expanded opportunities for prospects to engage with Michigan's academic leaders and one another.
Be a lead for our Dallas and Houston Campaign Councils during campaign periods.

Bachelor's degree or equivalent education and experience.
Five or more years of development experience in major gifts or other related fields like marketing, banking, or sales experience.
Sound knowledge of laws, practices, and philosophy of charitable giving.
Experience with financial development and/or sales productivity.
Experience working with and/or managing volunteers in some (preferably professional) capacity.

jobs.title: Director of Community Engagement, Alpha - $400,000/year USD
jobs.description:
"Alpha School students, on average, experience 2.4 to 2.6 times the academic growth of traditional school students"

— Forbes

Alpha is hiring.

The families who choose Alpha rarely arrive from an ad. They arrive because another family sat across from them at dinner and said, "This changed my kid." That word-of-mouth engine is the thing you would own for an entire region: the dinners, the parent ambassadors, the mayor's office, the CEO who opens a door for a 14-year-old's first real project.

A normal week puts you in four rooms. You design and host the region's calendar of gatherings, from a 150-person open house to an eight-seat curated dinner, several a month. You recruit current parents who genuinely want to talk to prospective ones and match them, family to family. You build relationships with city officials and business leaders, turning them into venues, sources of support for new campus openings, and real opportunities for students. And you deliver on the Alpha Networks: introductions, expert masterclasses, internships, alumni welcomes, logged family by family.

There is no finished playbook. You write it while running it, and the systems you invent get picked up by peers building the same engine in other cities. As the region grows, the scoreboard gets harder, not easier: doors opened per family has to rise even as enrollment climbs. Success shows up as the share of growth arriving through real people vouching for Alpha, read on a multi-year trend rather than a quarterly report.

No degree is required, and no particular pedigree. An MBA, a consulting or wealth-management career, and a self-made run in community, hospitality, or advancement all count the same here. What we read is the track record of convening people and turning those relationships into value.

This role is on-site in one of the following regions: San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, Denver, Greenwich, Miami, Atlanta, Boston, Oklahoma City, Tulsa, Dorado, Nashville, or Park City. Expect evenings and weekends in rooms full of high-expectation parents, elected officials, and founders, plus regular local travel. You will be the most connected person in your city, and you will spend that on kids. If that trade sounds like the point rather than the cost, apply.

What You Will Be Doing

Designing and running the region's gathering calendar: open events, curated dinners by city and grade, and family retreats, several a month and on budget
Securing venues, hosts, and vendors, then hosting the room live
Recruiting current parents as ambassadors, equipping them with true stories, and matching them to prospective families and tours
Opening relationships with public officials and business executives, and turning them into venues, campus-opening support, and student opportunities
Matching enrolled families into parent circles and students into mentorships, masterclasses, and real-world internships, and welcoming graduating families as alumni within 30 days
Logging every gathering, introduction, and first-contact attribution in the CRM (customer relationship management platform) so "doors opened per family" is a true number

What You Won’t Be Doing

Growth here is never bought — no paid media, no ad spend, no impression or lead-volume targets
Owning the brand story or top-down campaigns; Marketing has that
Processing admissions, running tours, or chasing enrollment paperwork; Admissions and Family Success have that
Running a campus day-to-day, or opening the physical building
Reporting raw attendance and headcount as if a full room were the result
Waiting for a finished playbook, a template, or support staff before you start

Director Of Community Engagement Key Responsibilities

Make people-first referrals the majority source of your region's enrollment growth.

Basic Requirements

5+ years building communities or relationship programs in K-12 education, membership, or a comparable network business, where growth came through people: referrals, members, congregations, chapters, alumni, or a client book, with numbers to show for it
Has personally designed and run 20+ gatherings across the full range, from intimate curated dinners to 100+ person open events, with budget ownership
Has opened and maintained relationships with public officials or business executives that produced concrete, nameable value
Disciplined CRM user; logging relationships, attributions, and actions is already a habit
Lives in, or will relocate to, one of these regions: San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, Denver, Greenwich (CT), Miami, Atlanta, Boston, Oklahoma City, Tulsa, Dorado (PR), Nashville, or Park City (UT)
Authorized to work in the US without visa sponsorship

Nice-to-have Requirements

Ran regional growth, community, or partnerships for a network-shaped organization: a school group, membership club, franchise, or faith or civic institution
Built and monetized a high-trust book of relationships as a client-facing principal in wealth management, consulting, or business development
Came up through admissions, advancement, community organizing, or hospitality, and were always the one asked to host and represent the institution
Existing relationships with local government or the business community in your city
Fluent in how families make high-stakes education decisions

About Alpha

Join the team building school around student growth

Alpha reimagines the school day around faster learning, stronger mentorship, and more time for students to build real-world skills.

Roles with real student impact:
Alpha hires teachers (guides), operators, admissions experts, school & curriculum leaders, and remote team members.

Education work that pays like it matters:
Alpha offers six-figure roles for people ready to help build a radically better school experience.

A culture built for builders:
Alpha is fast-moving, ambitious, and student focused. It’s for people who want to improve the system, not maintain it.

Alpha is where you can do the most meaningful work of your career.

There is so much to cover for this exciting role, and space here is limited. Hit the Apply button if you found this interesting and want to learn more. We look forward to meeting you!

Working with us

This is a full-time, W2 employee position with immediate access to benefits (https://support.crossover.com/article/7581-w2-benefits-u-s-paychex-paid-only). All roles are year-long positions. The compensation level for this role is $400,000 USD/year. The payment period is weekly. Consult www.crossover.com/help-and-faqs for more details on this topic.

jobs.title: Director of Operations
jobs.description:
It’s great to work at a place where people are truly committed to serving our students! We’re committed to bringing passion and energy to our College.

Visit our Life Page on LinkedIn to explore our dynamic campus culture, hear from current employees, and discover what makes Bucks County Community College a great place to work!

Bucks County Community College seeks a highly analytical, entrepreneurial, and operationally focused professional to serve as the Director of Operations for the Division of Workforce & Strategic Partnerships. Reporting directly to the Vice President of Workforce & Strategic Partnerships, this position serves as the division's senior operational leader responsible for improving operational effectiveness and advancing business performance through financial analysis, operational execution, utilization strategies, and performance management in support of priorities established by the Vice President.

The Director of Operations is responsible for the day-to-day operational leadership of the division and directly supervises the Associate Vice President of Workforce Development, the Executive Director of Community Education & Professional Certification, and the Executive Director of Corporate College & Customized Training. Through these leaders, the position ensures consistent execution of divisional priorities, operational accountability, and achievement of financial, enrollment, and performance objectives.

This position strengthens divisional performance through data-informed decision-making, business modeling, operational coordination, and continuous improvement. The Director supports revenue-generating programs through operational execution, financial analysis, and performance optimization while helping ensure the long-term financial sustainability of workforce, public safety, and community education programming.

Essential Functions

Business Performance

Support divisional revenue generating programs through operational execution, business analysis, and implementation of priorities established by divisional leadership.
Conduct market, enrollment, utilization, and operational analyses to identify opportunities to improve program performance, increase efficiency, and expand high-demand offerings.
Support implementation and operational optimization of divisional initiatives, programs, and revenue-generating activities through scheduling, utilization, pricing analysis, and performance monitoring.
Develop business cases, pricing analyses, and financial models to evaluate program feasibility, operational sustainability, and scalability.
Identify opportunities to maximize utilization of divisional facilities, classrooms, labs, and training centers, including evening, weekend, and year-round programming.
Evaluate program performance and recommend operational improvements to strengthen enrollment, resource utilization, earned revenue, and long-term sustainability.

Financial Strategy & Analytics

Lead financial and operational analyses to support divisional decision-making, resource allocation, and performance improvement.
Work with the Executive Director, Business Management to provide program-level financial and operational analyses, including cohort economics, program-level P&L analysis, cost-per-student and cost-per-completer analysis, revenue and margin performance, break-even modeling, enrollment forecasting, and scenario planning.
Develop multi-year financial projections and operational business models to support divisional planning.
Monitor divisional financial performance and provide recommendations to improve efficiency, sustainability, and operational outcomes.
Partner with the Finance Office to support budget development, forecasting, expense monitoring, financial reporting, and divisional planning.
Prepare executive-level reports, dashboards, and analyses for senior leadership, Cabinet discussions, Board reporting, and institutional planning efforts.
Provide financial and operational analysis to support workforce grants, funding proposals, and divisional investments.

Division Operations & Leadership

Provide direct leadership and supervision for the Community Education & Professional Certification, Workforce Development, and Corporate College & Customized Training units through the direct management of the Associate Vice President and Executive Directors responsible for these areas.
Translate the strategic direction established by the Vice President into operational plans and ensure consistent execution, accountability, and achievement of divisional goals.
Develop, streamline, document, and continuously improve operational systems, business processes, and cross-functional workflows to increase efficiency, accountability, responsiveness, and scalability across the division.
Direct operational planning for divisional facilities and training sites, including classroom and laboratory utilization, scheduling optimization, resource allocation, and space management.
Directly supervise the Associate Vice President of Workforce Development, the Executive Director of Community Education & Professional Certification, the Executive Director of Corporate College & Customized Training, and assigned operational and administrative personnel; establish performance expectations and foster a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, innovation, collaboration, and service excellence.
Monitor operational performance across all functional areas and work with divisional leaders to improve enrollment, revenue, customer service, operational effectiveness, and resource utilization.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in business administration, finance, public administration, workforce development, higher education administration, organizational leadership, or a related field.
Five (5) years of progressively responsible experience in operations, business performance, financial analysis, strategic implementation, or organizational leadership.
Demonstrated experience leading senior leaders and managing multi-unit operations.
Demonstrated experience supporting revenue-generating operations, financial modeling, program performance improvement, or business operations.
Strong analytical and financial skills with experience interpreting data to drive operational and business decisions.
Demonstrated ability to manage complex initiatives involving multiple stakeholders and competing priorities.
Exceptional communication, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
Demonstrated ability to work independently, exercise sound judgment, and operate effectively in a dynamic environment.
Proficiency with spreadsheets, dashboards, reporting tools, and enterprise administrative systems.

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree in business administration, organizational leadership, workforce development, finance, or a related discipline.
Experience in workforce development, continuing education, public safety training, or complex operational environments.
Experience with program-level financial management, P&L analysis, operational performance improvement, or business operations.
Knowledge of grants management, workforce funding, apprenticeship/pre-apprenticeship programs, and operational planning.
Experience with higher education or workforce technology systems, including Workday, Ellucian Colleague, Campus Marketplace, CRM systems, or workforce reporting tools.
Demonstrated success improving operational performance, supporting program growth, or enhancing earned revenue in a complex organization.

WORKING CONDITIONS

Standard office environment with regular travel between Bucks County Community College campuses and workforce training locations. Occasional evening and weekend work may be required to support workforce programs, public safety training, operational priorities, and divisional initiatives.

SALARY RANGE
$85,112 - $100,000 (commensurate with experience)

Benefits

Bucks County Community College offers an exceptional benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, prescription plans, 403B pension plan, life insurance, short & long-term disability, generous paid time off, tuition waivers, tuition assistance, wellness center, cafeteria, and free parking on a beautiful Bucks County campus.

BACKGROUND CHECKS/CLEARANCES

Employment with the College will require successful completion of background check(s) in accordance with College's policies.

APPLICATION

Apply online at: https://bucks.wd1.myworkdayjobs.com/BCCC

Applications must consist of a letter of application addressing this specific position and the candidate’s interest and qualifications for coming to Bucks County Community College, resume/CV, and professional references. References will not be contacted without prior permission. Finalists may be asked to provide additional materials.

DEADLINE

Applications will be accepted until the position is filled.

We are proud to be an organization that embraces the value of bringing diverse, talented, and committed people together. The fastest way to breakthrough innovation is when diverse ideas come together in an inclusive environment. We encourage our colleagues to respectfully challenge one another’s thinking and approach problems collectively. We are an equal opportunity employer, committed to fostering an inclusive and diverse workplace.

Please Note: At this time, the College does not provide work visa sponsorships. To be considered for employment at Bucks County Community College, applicants must be permitted to legally work in the United States without employer sponsorship. Bucks County Community College participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you are authorized to work in the U.S.

jobs.title: Executive Director - Senior Living
jobs.description:
Clearwater at The Arboretum
is looking for a seasoned leader looking for a new Executive Director
opportunity. Do you love changing lives for the better, collaborating with professionals to support seniors, building a dynamic and caring team, delivering great results in a beautiful environment? Then join us in our endeavor to create experiences that celebrate your relevance.

We welcome candidates with experience and a passion to make a difference in a senior's journey to aging.

Clearwater Living Associates Enjoy Great Benefits

Highly competitive salaries
Excellent benefits
401k + generous company match
Paid Vacation, Sick Days, Personal Holiday
Exciting opportunities to grow
Dynamic and fast paced environment
Culture of people first and service always

The Executive Director oversees and directs the day-to-day functions and efficient operations of the community, in accordance with all federal, state, local and licensing regulations, and all company policies and procedures. This role also ensures the highest quality of care for residents, while maintaining the community’s financial stability, and creating a harmonious working environment for all associates.

Responsibilities

Oversee, plan, develop, organize, implement, manage, control and direct all of the day-to-day functions and operations of the community including:
Consult with department directors on development and implementation of departmental policies and procedures
Establish rapport in and among departments to demonstrate, encourage and promote a spirit of teamwork and cooperation among associates
Identify and develop plan of corrections of problem areas to improve service to residents
Ensure compliance with all laws, regulations and legal requirements governing the community and all company policies and procedures
Ensure that all residents receive proper services with regard to their physical, mental & emotional needs
Conduct surveys and exit interviews to determine satisfaction levels and areas for improvement
Collaborate with the Director of Sales to promote and market the property within the local community by implementing referral and other programs, which are intended to reach full resident occupancy goals of the community
Responsible for overseeing all operations, finances and reporting including:
Approve all expenditures against budgets and maintain complete financial records including billing and accounts receivable
Maintain all required education units with complete understanding and knowledge of all Federal, State and Local government regulations, as well as trends within the industry
Ensure management team complies with all policies and procedures and maintains any required continuing education or licensing updates/requirements

jobs.description:
Remote – with preference of candidates in Nashville, TN, Knoxville, TN, or Birmingham, AL

DESCRIPTION:

The Parkinson's Foundation makes life better for people with Parkinson’s disease by improving care and advancing research toward a cure. In everything we do, we build on the energy, experience, and passion of our global Parkinson's community.

The Advancement Director will lead the Tennessee and Kentucky Chapter (TNKY) and Gulf Coast (GC) Chapter and be responsible for strategically implementing revenue development and mission delivery to advance the Parkinson’s Foundation’s goals. This role involves achieving targeted revenue metrics—such as fundraising events, corporate development, individual giving, and Ambassador/board development—and education & outreach metrics, including volunteer development, community partner engagement, and new outreach opportunities.

The Director will also develop, manage, and oversee the Chapter budget and long-term strategy for sustained revenue growth. Additionally, the Director will cultivate community partnerships and alliances to promote growth and awareness. As a key member of the regional team, the Advancement Director will collaborate with the Regional Director and other team members to meet regional standards and expectations.

RESPONSIBILITIES:
Responsibilities include, but are not limited to the following:

Revenue Generation and Outreach:

·      Drive revenue and outreach standards, strategies, and growth opportunities for the Chapters.
·      Develop, implement, contribute to, and monitor an annual budget and long-term strategy plan for the Chapter, including management of assigned chapter revenue benchmarks.
·      Formulate and implement strategies and tactics for Chapter fundraising activities to sustain continued growth, including optimizing opportunities in core market areas and identifying opportunities for expansion.
·      Build and execute a strategy for consistent Parkinson’s Foundation presence in remote communities served by the Chapter, including regular in-person travel by team to communities and strategically planned outreach activities.
·      Work with the team to create and implement strategies to meet fundraising goals through Parkinson’s Foundation’s signature Peer-to-Peer fundraising initiatives, including Moving Day events and special events. Provide hands-on support for P2P fundraising initiatives when necessary.

Stakeholder and Community Engagement:

·      Serve as lead relationship manager for key stakeholders both in revenue and mission delivery, including local community partners, corporate partners, allied health partners, and strategic partnerships.
·      Manage a personal portfolio of donors for cultivation, stewardship, and solicitation of increased giving. Sustain focus on increasing Chapter-level individual giving growth and work with revenue collaborators within the organization.
·      Develop and direct the cultivation, solicitation, follow-up, and recognition process for fundraising event participants, corporate partners, and key Chapter stakeholders year-round.
·      Actively seek opportunities to address community needs and positively impact the local community while advancing the mission, goals, and values.
·      Serve as a local representative for Parkinson’s Foundation, acting as spokesperson when necessary and appropriate.

Team and Volunteer Management:

·      Lead, recruit, and retain high-level volunteers and Ambassadors, including leadership of the Chapter Board and annual board giving.
·      Lead and coach (2) Chapter team members to achieve revenue, community outreach, and professional development success.

Operational Efficiency:

·      Maintain accurate records of Chapter activities and utilize the RE NXT database for community, donor, and constituent management.
·      Ensure total team compliance with organizational database tracking standards.
·      Perform all other duties and tasks required to support all new and/or proposed fundraising events, programs, and activities.
·      Stay informed about organization-wide activities and properly utilize available resources.
·      Be knowledgeable about Parkinson’s disease and the Foundation’s strategic plan and operations.

EXPERIENCE/SKILLS/QUALIFICATIONS REQUIRED:

Bachelor’s degree and a minimum of 6 years of fundraising experience, preferably within a healthcare non-profit organization.
Demonstrated track record of successful fundraising experience that includes special events, corporate/foundation giving, donor cultivation and recognition, donor records, and acknowledgment.
Proven and applicable skills in strategic planning, budgeting, and volunteer development.
Outgoing, energetic, organized, and detail-oriented team member who can adhere to timelines and prioritize effectively.
Strong verbal and written communication and presentation skills.
Skilled people developer with a history of managing high-performing teams of 2 or more.
Ability to lead and close high-level solicitations.
Excellent interpersonal and relationship-building skills.
Strong volunteer recruitment, committee development, and management skills.
Experience securing corporate partnerships is a must.
Self-starter who is also collaborative, a quick learner, and an effective team player.
Excellent active listening, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
Ability to effectively multi-task, establish priorities, and work in a fast-paced environment.
Highly efficient in time management and able to meet deadlines under pressure. Detail-oriented with strong organizational skills.
Ability to provide a high level of customer service to external constituents.
Self-motivated, results-oriented leader with strong organizational skills.
Strong computer skills, proficient with the MS Office suite.
Proficiency in Raiser’s Edge NXT is a plus.
Must be able to lift at least 20 lbs. from the ground to waist level with or without reasonable accommodation.

·      Capacity to work flexible hours, including evenings and weekends, with adherence to core business hours.
·      Ability to travel throughout the Chapter and region up to 30% of the time, with reliable personal transportation and a valid driver’s license.
·      Demonstrates the organizational values of excellence, teamwork, collaboration, integrity, positivity, dedication and responsiveness.

COMPENSATION:

Salary for this position is competitive and depends on prior experience. In addition, a comprehensive benefits package is included. The salary range for this position is $70,000-$80,000

Please submit a resume, cover letter, and salary requirement to cantol@parkinson.org. Applicant review will continue until the position is filled. Please indicate, “Advancement Director – TNKY Chapter”
in the subject line. Resumes without a cover letter and salary requirements will not be considered. No phone calls please.

jobs.description:
ROLE TITLE: Managing Director, Account Management, National Corporate Partnerships
(Full-time)

POSITION REPORTS TO: Jerry Ochoa, Vice President, National Corporate Partnerships

PRIORITY APPLICATION DEADLINE: Sep 1, 2026 at 11:59PM ET

LOCATION: Flexible

What You'll Do

We are looking for a Managing Director, Account Management to lead Teach For America's national corporate account management portfolio and drive the retention, deepening, and expansion of our current corporate partnerships. In this role, you will set the vision, strategy, and stewardship approach that keep our most important corporate partners closely engaged with TFA's mission, and you will personally manage a portfolio of six- and seven-figure partners. While net-new corporate partner acquisition sits with the MD, Business Development, this role owns the expansion and upsell of existing partnerships — including converting current partners into larger, multi-year, and transformational investors.

The ideal candidate will be passionate about building durable, mission-aligned partnerships with senior corporate leaders and translating those relationships into sustained, multi-year investments. You bring a best-in-class customer service orientation, a rigorous attention to detail, strong strategic thinking, and the ability to take a bird's-eye view of the portfolio while attending to any and all needs of each corporate partner. You bring curiosity and openness to how emerging technologies — particularly AI — can accelerate your work, and you approach these tools with fluency, critical thinking, and a strong ethical grounding.

The goal for this role in particular is to retain and grow TFA's existing corporate revenue base by delivering exceptional partner experiences that convert current partners into long-term, transformational investors.

What You'll Be Responsible For

Portfolio Strategy and Vision (20%)

Set the annual and multi-year strategy for the corporate account management portfolio, including national and nationally-managed revenue goals.
Develop annual priorities and tactics designed to retain, deepen, and grow current corporate partners.
Build and maintain the account management team's infrastructure, KPIs, and workflow management processes.

Portfolio Management and Partner Stewardship (40%)

Lead a portfolio of six- and seven-figure corporate partners at the national and regional levels.
Serve as primary strategist and central relationship manager for TFA's current corporate partners.
Serve as the primary external representative of TFA with current corporate donors, including engagement with C-suite leaders, corporate foundation executives, and CSR/ESG heads.
Oversee, strategize, and/or execute on general fundraising operations and stewardship of corporate funders, including renewals, impact reporting, and recognition.
Ensure newly closed partners are successfully transitioned from the Business Development sub-team, delivering a best-in-class donor experience across the partnership lifecycle.

Cross-Functional Collaboration and Enterprise Development (15%)

Forge and foster deep partnerships with regional fundraising teams and national colleagues to build mutually beneficial engagement strategies that meet partner priorities and TFA's priorities.
Leverage TFA's network of national and regional board members, senior leaders, and program teams to retain and grow current partners.
Contribute to enterprise-wide development mindsets and donor-centered strategies across TFA.
Lead complex, cross-functional project management to deliver on partnership commitments — managing down, across, and up within the organization and with external partners.
Explore, develop, and responsibly apply AI tools to strengthen partner stewardship, portfolio management, and internal workflows — modeling curious, ethical, and critically-minded use of emerging technology for the sub-team and the broader NCPT.

People Management and Team Culture (15%)

Manage and develop your direct report (for our current fiscal year this will likely mean managing one Director on the Account Management sub-team) toward their annual retention and growth goals.
Onboard, coach, and empower direct reports to grow as professional fundraisers and to meet their portfolio and revenue targets.
Build an equitable and inclusive sub-team culture within Account Management that reflects TFA's core values.
Support the professional growth and long-term trajectory of direct reports.

Contribution to Team, Development, and Organizational Culture (10%)

Contribute to a collective culture of excellence, teamwork, Core Values leadership, and commitment to DEI on the NCPT, National Development Team, and across the organization.
Participate in special projects (e.g., economic model sprints, cross-team initiatives such as the Lead Now Fund).
Step into leadership and facilitation opportunities at the Development team and organization level.
Speak with respect and courage when necessary to improve processes, culture, and mindsets aligned to TFA's Foundations and Core Values.

A WEEK IN THE LIFE

Over the course of any week, the Managing Director, Account Management will spend time:

Preparing for and leading stewardship, renewal, and growth conversations with senior executives at current corporate partners.
Coaching direct reports on portfolio strategy, partner communications, and renewal execution.
Building and refining impact reports, renewal proposals, and other high-stakes partner-facing materials.
Experimenting with and applying AI tools to accelerate research, drafting, analysis, and preparation — and sharing learnings with the team.
Partnering with the VP, NCPT and MD, Business Development to align on team goals, portfolio health, and cross-sub-team handoffs.
Collaborating with regional fundraising leaders on shared partners and cross-cutting opportunities.
Tracking portfolio activity, retention rates, and revenue projections in Salesforce and other reporting tools.
Representing TFA at partner-facing events, executive briefings, and stewardship convenings.

Your Experience

Your areas of knowledge and expertise that matter most for this role (minimum qualifications):

Ability to build and manage a high-performing corporate account management function, from strategy through execution.
Expertise in the corporate philanthropy, corporate social responsibility, and/or corporate partnerships landscape.
Strong strategic thinking, with the ability to identify opportunities to deepen and grow existing partnerships.
Proficient in senior-level relationship management, including engaging with C-suite executives and corporate foundation leaders.
Best-in-class customer service orientation and rigorous attention to detail.
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, including proposal writing, executive briefings, and impact reporting.
Rigorous project and portfolio management skills, with the ability to manage many complex partnerships simultaneously.
Strong people management skills and ability to develop direct reports.
Deep commitment to TFA's mission, values, and commitment to Diversity, Equity, and Inclusiveness.
Education: Bachelor's degree required.
Proficient in Microsoft Office; experience with Salesforce required.
Curiosity and openness to emerging technologies — including AI tools — with the fluency, critical thinking, and ethical grounding to explore, evaluate, and responsibly apply them in daily work.

BONUS (preferred Qualifications)

Prior Experience

At least 7 years of fundraising experience, partnership management, or account management experience with a strong track record of retaining and growing six- and seven-figure relationships.
Prior management experience, including managing to ambitious retention and revenue goals.
Experience in the education sector or in mission-driven nonprofit fundraising.
Experience navigating complex, national organizations with matrixed local and central teams.
CFRE (Certified Fund-Raising Executive) certification, MBA, or other advanced degree preferred.

Work Demands

Travel up to 3–4x per quarter for internal and external meetings.
Occasional evening and weekend work required to support high-stakes cultivation and stewardship activities.

Skills

Ability to take a bird's-eye view of the portfolio while attending to any and all details of each partner.
Ability to be entrepreneurial and flexible in a fast-paced, results-oriented culture.
Strong ability to influence others toward outcomes without direct authority.
Positive, can-do approach and ability to bring hopefulness and optimism to the team.
Prior experience integrating AI tools into fundraising, sales, communications, research, or knowledge management workflows.

YOUR FUTURE TEAM

The National Corporate Partnerships Team (NCPT) is one of five sub-teams on TFA's National Development Team. Our charge is to strengthen, grow, and create new corporate partnerships that maximize financial and broader contributions to TFA's mission and long-term sustainability. The Account Management sub-team is responsible for the retention, deepening, and expansion of TFA's existing corporate partner portfolio, working in close partnership with the Business Development sub-team, regional fundraisers, and enterprise-wide leaders. Under a five-person structure of VP + 2 MDs + 2 Directors, this MD will lead the Account Management function and directly shape TFA's most important, long-standing corporate relationships. NCPT is an AI-forward sub-team, actively exploring how emerging technology can deepen partner relationships, sharpen strategy, and expand our capacity — and we're looking for leaders who share that curiosity.

jobs.title: Chief Operating Officer
jobs.description:
Who We Are

Rowe Plastic Surgery (RPS)
is a multi-site aesthetic and reconstructive plastic surgery practice with locations in Montclair, NJ; Red Bank, NJ; New York (Park Avenue and 77th Street); and Palm Beach, FL. RPS is privately owned, with no board of directors, strategic and operating decisions are made in direct partnership with Ownership. RPS has built a strong regional reputation and a loyal patient base and is now entering its next phase of growth: professionalizing its infrastructure, scaling beyond a single-specialty model, and positioning the organization for institutional capital, joint venture partnerships, and/or a future transaction.

Position Summary

RPS is seeking a Chief Executive Officer
to be based in West Palm Beach Headquarters to lead the organization through its next stage of growth from an approximately 50-employee, founder-driven practice into a scaled, multi-platform healthcare organization. Reporting directly to Ownership, and partnering closely with the COO, VP of Human Resources, and Senior Financial Analyst, the CEO will serve as the senior-most operating executive of RPS, with full accountability for the organization in the absence of a formal board. The CEO will be responsible for both setting strategy and personally driving execution: building the operational backbone required to support growth, expanding RPS's service lines and market footprint beyond plastics and reconstructive surgery (including adjacent platforms such as IVF/fertility), and pursuing growth through joint ventures, M&A, and organic expansion. A core mandate of this role is to make RPS an attractive, well-run, and defensible platform for private equity investment or an eventual sale without sacrificing clinical quality, physician alignment, or patient experience along the way.

Core CEO Functions

Standard general-management responsibilities that come with sole executive accountability in a privately held company with no board:
•     Own overall P&L performance and financial results for the entire organization, across all sites and service lines.
•     Set organizational vision, mission, and long-term strategic direction in direct partnership with Ownership.
•     Serve as final decision-maker on major operational, financial, and strategic matters -sound independent judgment and clear communication with Ownership are essential.
•     Build, lead, and hold accountable the senior leadership team, including the COO, VP of HR, and Senior Financial Analyst, and define future executive hires (e.g., CFO) as the organization scales.
•     Ensure regulatory, legal, and clinical compliance across all sites and jurisdictions (NY, NJ, FL, GA).
•     Oversee financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, and internal controls, partnering closely with the Senior Financial Analyst (or future CFO)
•     Direct organizational design and talent strategy in partnership with the VP of HR, including workforce planning as RPS scales.
•     Own day-to-day operational performance in partnership with the COO, ensuring strategy translates into consistent execution at the site level.
•     Manage risk across the organization financial, operational, clinical, and reputational.
•     Represent RPS externally to physicians, patients, vendors, lenders, and potential investors or partners.
•     Allocate capital and resources across existing sites, new markets, and growth initiatives.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Strategy & Platform Growth

•     Develop and execute a multi-year growth strategy that scales RPS from its current single-specialty footprint into a diversified, multi-platform healthcare organization.
•     Identify and evaluate expansion into adjacent, complementary healthcare verticals (e.g., IVF/fertility, med spa, dermatology, wellness) that leverage RPS's brand, patient base, and referral relationships.
•     Define and prioritize new market entry, new geographies, new sites, and new service lines, based on demand, competitive dynamics, and return on investment.
•     Translate strategy into an actionable execution roadmap with clear milestones, ownership, and accountability, this is a builder/operator role, not a strategy-only mandate.

M&A, Joint Ventures & Capital Strategy

•     Lead sourcing, evaluation, negotiation, and integration of acquisition targets, joint ventures, and strategic partnerships that accelerate platform growth.
•     Understand and apply healthcare company valuation methodologies to assess acquisition targets, partnership structures, and RPS's own enterprise value over time.
•     Prepare RPS operationally and financially to be an attractive platform for private equity investment, recapitalization, or sale, including data room readiness, KPI infrastructure, and de-risking key-person dependencies.
•     Build and manage relationships with investment bankers, private equity sponsors, legal counsel, and other transaction advisors as RPS evaluates capital and exit options.
•     Design and execute go-to-market strategies for new service lines, locations, and partnerships, including positioning, channel strategy, and competitive differentiation.

Operational Leadership

•     In close partnership with the COO — not limited to financial projections and analysis but support the operational execution as required.
•     Partner closely with the COO, VP of HR, Senior Financial Analyst, clinical, and site leadership to ensure strategy translates into consistent execution at the practice level.
•     Establish and monitor KPIs and operating metrics across sites and service lines, driving accountability and continuous improvement.
•     Evaluate and implement technology, workflow, and process improvements that increase efficiency, patient experience, and margin as RPS scales.

Physician & Provider Compensation

•     Design, structure, and evolving physician and provider compensation models that align incentives with production, quality, patient experience, and organizational growth goals.
•     Benchmark physician compensation against market and specialty norms across plastics, reconstructive, and any newly added service lines.
•     Structure compensation approaches that support recruitment and retention of high-performing physicians while remaining sustainable and defensible in a future transaction or partnership.
•     Partner with HR and legal/compliance on physician contracts, productivity models, and equity or partnership structures where applicable.

Organizational Leadership & Culture

•     Build out an executive and operational leadership team capable of supporting a rapidly scaling, multi-site organization, including future roles (e.g., CFO) as RPS grows.
•     Partner with the VP of HR to formalize infrastructure — policies, compliance, talent, and culture — appropriate for a growth-stage healthcare platform.
•     Serve as the primary external face of RPS with investors, partners, physicians, and key stakeholders, while maintaining the culture and patient-first values that built the practice.
 QUALIFICATIONS

Required

Steward a culture of Philanthropy at all levels of the agency, including amongst staff, senior leadership, and Board of Directors.

jobs.title: Senior Director of Development
jobs.description:
Position Summary

Joshua Nations is seeking a full-time Senior Development Director
to lead the ministry’s donor development strategy, expand financial partnerships, strengthen donor relationships, and help increase the organization’s long-term revenue capacity.

The Development Director will serve as the senior leader responsible for development strategy, major donor cultivation, donor pipeline management, campaigns, church and business partnerships, and coordination of the development team. This role will work closely with the President/CEO, Grant Writer, Director of Impact Reporting, COO, International Director, Creative Team, and Board of Directors to build a disciplined and sustainable development system.

Joshua Nations’ long-term goal is to increase annual revenue from approximately $1.6 million to $3 million
. The Development Director will play a central role in helping achieve this growth through major gifts, donor upgrades, recurring giving, grant support, strategic campaigns, church partnerships, business partnerships, and new donor acquisition.

Compensation

Salary range: $90,000–$120,000 plus benefits
, commensurate with experience, proven fundraising ability, donor network, leadership capacity, and strategic development expertise.
Joshua Nations may also consider performance-based bonuses or compensation growth tied to clear development goals, healthy donor development practices, and measurable revenue growth.
Joshua Nations does not use commission-based fundraising compensation. Any incentive structure will be designed to honor ethical, relationship-based, ministry-centered fundraising.

Purpose of the Role

The Development Director exists to build and lead a comprehensive development strategy that increases Joshua Nations’ financial capacity while strengthening donor trust, mission alignment, and long-term partnership.

This role is not simply administrative. It is a senior-level, frontline development position requiring relational warmth, strategic thinking, disciplined follow-through, confidence in making financial asks, and the ability to represent Joshua Nations with excellence to donors, churches, businesses, foundations, and ministry partners.

The Development Director will help move Joshua Nations from founder/President-centered fundraising toward a scalable development system that supports continued growth and ministry impact.

Growth Pathway

This role is initially structured as a Development Director
position rather than a Chief Development Officer position because Joshua Nations is still building its formal development infrastructure. The Development Director will be expected to lead and execute donor development strategy, cultivate major gifts, strengthen donor relationships, and produce measurable revenue growth.

As fundraising goals are met and the development function expands, this position may grow into a Chief Development Officer
role. Promotion to Chief Development Officer would be considered based on demonstrated fundraising success, achievement of agreed revenue benchmarks, ability to build scalable development systems, leadership capacity, and the need to hire and manage additional development personnel.

If the Development Director successfully helps Joshua Nations reach its revenue goals, Joshua Nations may build a development team under this role. This pathway is intended to give the right candidate room to grow with the organization while ensuring that future title changes and team expansion are tied to proven results, organizational need, and sustainable revenue growth.

Key Revenue Deliverables

The Development Director will be expected to produce measurable fundraising results.

Required Return-on-Investment Goals

Within 12 Months

The Development Director should raise or directly influence at least 2x their annual base salary
in new revenue, increased giving, or committed pledges.
Based on the salary range, this equals approximately:
$180,000
if salary is $90,000
$240,000
if salary is $120,000

jobs.title: Director of Development - Meritus College
jobs.description:
The Organization: Merit America

The American economy is broken. Today, 53 million working adults–nearly half of the U.S. workforce–do not earn a living wage. These talented workers have few options to advance: college is too long and expensive, full-time boot camp programs don't offer enough flexibility, and online courses don't have the structure or support to translate learning into a new career. The result? Talented workers, disproportionately people of color and women, get stuck in low-wage roles with no way to build a better life for themselves and their families.

Merit America is a national nonprofit that creates pathways to family-sustaining careers for Americans stuck in low-wage work. Our fast, flexible solutions are built for working adults: We start by analyzing tens of millions of job postings to identify in-demand, high-paying tech careers and then work with industry-recognized partners to train for these roles with part-time programs that combine flexible online learning with best-in-class coaching. Finally, we support our learners in their job search, helping them connect with a broad constellation of local and national employers such as JPMorgan Chase and Infosys to land higher-earning, family-sustaining jobs. Merit America is on a mission to build a scalable pathway for workers to join the middle class through merit, not money. Since our founding in 2018, we've generated a projected $1 billion in near-term wage gains for our learners.

The Organization: Meritus College

Meritus College is a new kind of not-for-profit online college, built from the ground up to meet the needs of working adults and career-changers who've been overlooked by traditional higher education.

The problem is clear: only 33% of Pell grant recipients complete their degrees at two-year colleges within 6 years. College has become too rigid, too expensive, and too disconnected from both student realities and career outcomes. Merit College is different. Our online, asynchronous programs and "workplace as laboratory" approach allow students to learn and apply new skills directly to their jobs, while receiving personalized support from dedicated coaches every step of the way. We focus on real-world skills and stackable credentials in high-demand fields, ensuring graduates are prepared for today's jobs and tomorrow's opportunities. Founded in 2025 with an inaugural Associate of Applied Science in Technology and Innovation degree, Merit College is building a mainstream pathway to economic mobility—one designed not for the privileged few, but for the talented many who've too often been left behind.

About The Role

Meritus College doesn't have a century of alumni wealth to call on. What it has is a bold, evidence-backed model, a founding team with credibility in both higher ed and philanthropy, and an open field for building a modern fundraising function that looks more like an early-stage nonprofit startup than a traditional university advancement office.

We're looking for a Director of Development to join this founding team and help build that function. This is a hybrid role: part traditional higher-ed philanthropy (institutional funders and individual donors who care about post-secondary access and attainment), part startup-style fundraising (moving fast, building processes as you go, wearing multiple hats, working with founders, and engaging funders in the mission first - not the endowment).

A successful candidate will:

Manage and expand a portfolio of mission-aligned 6- and 7-figure foundation, corporate, and individual funders who care about economic mobility and the future of higher education.
Translate Meritus College's early outcomes data and founding story (which includes Merit America's success to date) into compelling, fundable narratives.
Move comfortably between the discipline of traditional higher-ed philanthropy (stewardship, reporting, gift agreements) and the speed and resourcefulness of an early-stage startup.
Lead the fundraising strategy to launch Meritus College. Beyond direct portfolio management, this work will include shaping and building new fundraising initiatives and ways of working that meet the needs of a new, innovative higher education model.

This role reports to the Managing Director of Development and works closely with Merit America's broader Development Team and Meritus College's academic and operating leadership.

What You'll Be Doing

The primary responsibilities of the Director of Development will include, but are not limited to, the following:

Build and Advance the Pipeline (50%)

Identify, research, and cultivate new funding relationships across foundations, corporate partners, and individual donors who care about higher-ed innovation and economic mobility, bearing in mind that Meritus College does not have an alumni base to draw from.
Lead proposal development with support from Merit America's Development team, adapting fundraising narratives as Meritus College's model, outcomes, and proof points evolve.
Bring an entrepreneurial lens to prospecting: apply the kind of hustle, creativity, and resourcefulness common in early-stage startup fundraising to a philanthropic context.
Track and analyze pipeline health, funder trends, and outcomes to continuously sharpen strategy.

Manage Donor and Prospect Relationships (30%)

Lead a small portfolio of existing warm prospects and new 6- and 7-figure funding relationships, managing the full cycle from first outreach through solicitation, close, and stewardship – with a goal of advancing $10M in deals to proposal stage (or later) in your first year, with support from the broader Development Team.
Write clear, engaging correspondence that connects Meritus College's data and mission to what funders care about.
Represent Meritus College in funder meetings and presentations, including opportunities to bring in founders/academic leadership for key relationships.
Ensure funders are stewarded and renewed thoughtfully to build long-term trust in a startup college reimagining higher education from the inside out.

Build the Function (20%)

Partner with Meritus College's academic, data, and operations teams to gather the proof points and impact data funders will want to see.
In collaboration with Meritus College leadership, build the advancement function - bringing your expertise and perspectives on how a startup-minded fundraising function should look different from a traditional university advancement office.

What Makes a Successful Candidate

We recognize that people from underrepresented backgrounds are often less likely to apply unless they meet every qualification. Don't let that be the reason you miss out — we encourage you to apply if you demonstrate many, not all, of the following:

Must Haves

Experience Building New Programs in Higher Education

Experience as the fundraising lead, or the close partner to the fundraising lead, on something a college or university was building for the first time: a new degree program, school, campus, institute, accredited entity, or a nonprofit incubated inside an institution.
Working knowledge of accreditation, credit portability and transfer, academic model design, and the diligence institutional funders run on a new or newly accredited program.
Track record of raising money or building partnerships, or of supporting the person or team who did. Familiar with what it takes to build a case for support while the proof points are still accumulating.

Note: we're open to candidates who came to this from the academic, program, or operations side and partnered closely with development. Deep involvement in building a new academic offering, alongside the fundraisers making the case for it, counts here.

Entrepreneurial & Startup Mindset

Bias for action: willing to prospect cold, draft the first version of a proposal template, and figure it out rather than wait for a fully formed process, while working quickly and collaboratively with the development team, college team, and executive leadership. You are self-directed and make good calls with incomplete information.
Genuine comfort with ambiguity: this is a new college inside a growing organization, so strategy, goals, and the pitch itself will shift as we learn. A target funder list may need rebuilding after a new data point comes in. We need someone who finds that energizing.
Track record of leveraging resources including AI to speed up and make more efficient tasks like research, drafting, and prospecting so a small team can punch above its weight.

Communication & Storytelling

Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate data and mission into a persuasive case for support.
Comfort with pitching a new institution with credibility and honesty about what's proven and what's still being built.
Confidence shaping an ambiguous narrative with prospective funders, including thinking with agility and creativity in conversations.

Mission Alignment

Genuine belief in expanding access to higher education for working adults and non-traditional students, and enthusiasm for a model that looks different from a traditional four-year college.
Alignment with Merit America's values: Think Big, Deliver Results, Win & Lose Together, Learn Constantly, Care Deeply, Enjoy the Ride.

Nice to Have

Direct experience at a startup, scaling nonprofit, or other fast-moving, resource-constrained organization — comfortable operating without established playbooks, and energized by building rather than maintaining.
Existing relationships with foundations or funders focused on postsecondary attainment, workforce development, or economic mobility.
Experience with Salesforce or a comparable CRM.
Comfort using AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT) to speed up research, drafting, and prospecting.

Other Logistics

This position is full-time: 4-day work week (Fridays are an operating day if there is a holiday closure during the week)
Travel:
Occasional travel required (up to 25% of time)

We compare our benchmarks against similarly sized non-profit organizations with comparable annual budgets and geographical areas. jobs.description:
Director of Development – School of Law

Are you a relationship-builder who thrives on connecting donor passions with transformational impact? The UND Alumni Association & Foundation is seeking a Director of Development to lead major gift fundraising efforts for the School of Law.

In this role, you'll partner closely with the Dean, faculty, and university leadership to identify, cultivate, and solicit major and planned gifts that advance the mission of the School of Law and the University of North Dakota. You'll manage a portfolio of high-capacity donors, develop meaningful engagement strategies, and inspire philanthropic investment through personalized outreach and compelling proposals.
We're looking for a motivated, strategic fundraiser who excels at building relationships, and communicating the value of higher education.

If you're ready to help shape the future of legal education through philanthropy, we'd love to hear from you.
POSITION SUMMARY
Reporting to the Vice President of Development, the Director of Development will work closely with the Dean of the School of Law and faculty to enhance and support their fundraising efforts. This position is primarily responsible for the qualification, cultivation and solicitation of individual prospects capable of giving in excess of $25,000. The Director of Development will be responsible for major gifts fundraising within the School of Law and UND, including arranging cultivation and solicitation visits with individuals, corporations, foundations and the development of proposals for private funding. This position is responsible for expanding the organization’s donor base by forging new relationships with potential donors of all levels. The Director of Development is responsible for building and maintaining a portfolio of 90-120 and major gift prospects and soliciting them for multi-year pledges. The Director of Development will actively engage the prospects in the portfolio and schedule approximately 100-125 personal visits annually.

Qualify, cultivate, solicit and close major and planned gifts from individuals, corporations, foundations, and friends to reach predetermined goal while maintaining and growing existing relationships to benefit UND.

Traveling regionally and nationally as well as attend evening, weekend activities, and appropriate events, programs and meetings.

jobs.description:
ART MUSEUM (BL-AMUS-IUBLA)

Since its establishment in 1941, the Sidney and Lois Eskenazi Museum of Art at Indiana University (IU) has grown from a small university teaching collection into one of the foremost university art museums in the country. A preeminent teaching museum, its internationally acclaimed collection includes more than 48,000 objects representing nearly every art-producing culture throughout history. Collection areas include African art, ancient art, Asian art, global contemporary art, European and American Art, Indigenous art, Oceanic art, and prints, drawings, and photography.

The Associate Director of Development designs and implements engagement and solicitation strategies for the Eskenazi Museum of Art¿s donors, and prospective donors.

The Opportunity

As Executive Director, Product Lifecycle & Membership Marketing, you will lead product marketers to acquire new accounts, shape and implement product-specific marketing strategies, focus on performance metrics, and deliver measurable results. You will accelerate growth through continuous test-and-learn agenda, improvement of paid marketing efforts, and expert allocation of marketing investments. Your team will ideate, plan, launch, measure, and optimize marketing campaigns to drive sustainable growth at efficient Cost Per Account (CPAs). You will be accountable for a large marketing budget, and you will collaborate closely with internal stakeholders such as Brand, Product, Risk, and Analytics to drive growth via both new-to-USAA members as well as cross-selling to existing members. Strong analytical skills, business acumen, and entrepreneurial spirit are key to success in this role.

jobs.title: Director of Community Engagement, Alpha - $400,000/year USD
jobs.description:
"Alpha School students, on average, experience 2.4 to 2.6 times the academic growth of traditional school students"

— Forbes

Alpha is hiring.

The families who choose Alpha rarely arrive from an ad. They arrive because another family sat across from them at dinner and said, "This changed my kid." That word-of-mouth engine is the thing you would own for an entire region: the dinners, the parent ambassadors, the mayor's office, the CEO who opens a door for a 14-year-old's first real project.

A normal week puts you in four rooms. You design and host the region's calendar of gatherings, from a 150-person open house to an eight-seat curated dinner, several a month. You recruit current parents who genuinely want to talk to prospective ones and match them, family to family. You build relationships with city officials and business leaders, turning them into venues, sources of support for new campus openings, and real opportunities for students. And you deliver on the Alpha Networks: introductions, expert masterclasses, internships, alumni welcomes, logged family by family.

There is no finished playbook. You write it while running it, and the systems you invent get picked up by peers building the same engine in other cities. As the region grows, the scoreboard gets harder, not easier: doors opened per family has to rise even as enrollment climbs. Success shows up as the share of growth arriving through real people vouching for Alpha, read on a multi-year trend rather than a quarterly report.

No degree is required, and no particular pedigree. An MBA, a consulting or wealth-management career, and a self-made run in community, hospitality, or advancement all count the same here. What we read is the track record of convening people and turning those relationships into value.

This role is on-site in one of the following regions: San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, Denver, Greenwich, Miami, Atlanta, Boston, Oklahoma City, Tulsa, Dorado, Nashville, or Park City. Expect evenings and weekends in rooms full of high-expectation parents, elected officials, and founders, plus regular local travel. You will be the most connected person in your city, and you will spend that on kids. If that trade sounds like the point rather than the cost, apply.

What You Will Be Doing

Designing and running the region's gathering calendar: open events, curated dinners by city and grade, and family retreats, several a month and on budget

jobs.title: Director of Community Engagement, 2 Hour Learning - $400,000/year USD
jobs.description:
You went into private school leadership to shape how children learn, not to run capital campaigns and referee parent committees. There is a version of this job where the academic model is protected for you, operations is handled centrally, and you spend your week on what you are best at: winning over the families who matter most, turning them into advocates, and being the voice of authority when the conversation gets hard.

You will own the parent side of Alpha in one metro — Miami, San Francisco, or Los Angeles. Your measure is enrollment and advocacy: prospective ultra-high-net-worth families who convert, current UHNW families who re-enroll, refer, and publicly champion 2 Hour Learning, and a local community where Alpha is top of mind. Roughly half your week is outward-facing — community partnerships, info sessions, and 1:1 conversations with sophisticated parents who have read every AI skeptic and want to know why the model actually works.

The rest of the seat is the escalation line. When an Associate Dean of Parents reaches the edge of what they can resolve — a board family threatening to pull their kids, a campus quietly softening the model to keep a vocal parent happy — it comes to you. You retain the family and you keep the model intact. Both. Then you document the precedent so the Associate Dean network can handle it next time without you.

If you have run a private or independent K-12 school, or you have spent a career earning the trust of UHNW families in another industry, and you have been waiting for the job where judgment and persuasion are the actual deliverables, this is it.

What You Will Be Doing

Building local awareness through partnerships with family offices, private clubs, and independent advisors, plus workshops and community events that generate inbound interest
Running admissions for wealthy families end to end: info sessions, 1:1 follow-up in the CRM, and the enrollment decision, including telling a family this is not the right school for their child
Turning enrolled parents into public champions of 2 Hour Learning through advocacy workshops and parent-to-parent networks, so enrolled families become your strongest source of new inquiries
Resolving the escalations others cannot: diagnosing whether the problem is the model, campus execution, or family fit, engaging the family directly, then writing up the precedent for the rest of the network
Keeping current families close through regular touchpoints, and reporting the patterns you hear back to leadership

What You Won’t Be Doing

Fundraising of any kind is off your plate — no capital campaigns, donor cultivation, or major gifts
Convening PTAs, School Improvement Councils, parent committees, or focus groups that get a vote on school policy
Managing facilities, finance, legal, vendors, technology, marketing, or community logistics — centralized teams own all of this, so your week stays on relationships, not operations
Designing curriculum or coaching instructional staff on pedagogy; the academic model is owned and protected centrally
Making exceptions or customizations to the educational model to satisfy a parent request, however influential the parent
Simply logging and responding to complaints, or writing newsletters and routine parent communications
Defusing conflict by avoiding it — diplomacy here means delivering hard messages, not softening standards
