Director of Operations – High-Voltage Transmission

Location:
Fort Worth, TX
Travel:
Approximately 3 days per week throughout Texas
Project Focus:
765kV High-Voltage Transmission
Compensation:
Competitive base salary + MBO incentive program
Additional Benefits:
Company truck provided

Position Overview A leading electrical utility contractor is conducting a confidential search for an experienced Director of Operations
to support major high-voltage transmission construction projects across Texas.
This position will play a key operational leadership role on a significant 765kV transmission program
. Candidates with substantial 345kV or 500kV transmission construction experience
will also be considered.

The ideal candidate will come directly from the utility contractor/EPC construction environment
and have hands-on experience managing the operational and financial performance of large, complex transmission projects. This position requires a strong combination of PMO leadership, P&L management, contract management, scheduling, project controls, and field operations experience
.

This is intended to be a hands-on Director-level operations position rather than an executive-level corporate role. Candidates should be comfortable working closely with project teams and field leadership while maintaining accountability for project financial and operational performance.

Key Responsibilities Provide operational leadership for large-scale high-voltage transmission construction projects
, including a major 765kV program.
Maintain responsibility for project P&L performance
, including budgets, forecasting, margins, cost-to-complete, and overall financial results.
Lead and support PMO functions
within a utility construction environment, ensuring consistent project controls, reporting, forecasting, and execution standards.
Oversee projects generally ranging from $50M–$100M+
in value.
Manage project schedules and ensure alignment between field production, manpower, procurement, subcontractors, equipment, and client milestones.
Provide oversight of contract management
, including contract requirements, commercial terms, change management, scope management, and risk mitigation.
Work closely with project controls teams to monitor cost, schedule, productivity, forecasting, and project performance
.
Lead Project Managers, Construction Managers, Superintendents, and other operational personnel.
Identify project risks and implement corrective actions before they negatively impact schedule, cost, or client commitments.
Ensure appropriate manpower, equipment, materials, and subcontractor resources are aligned with project requirements.
Partner with executive leadership on operational strategy, project performance, resource planning, and client expectations.
Maintain strong relationships with utility clients while representing the perspective and commercial interests of the contractor.
Conduct regular project and site visits throughout Texas.
Drive accountability across safety, quality, schedule, cost, productivity, and profitability.

Baseline Qualifications Candidates should have a strong combination of the following experience:
Utility contractor experience is required.
Candidates whose backgrounds are primarily on the utility/owner side without significant contractor-side construction experience will not be the best fit.
Demonstrated PMO experience within a utility construction contractor or EPC organization
.
Strong P&L management experience
, with direct accountability for project financial performance, margins, forecasting, and cost control.
Significant contract management experience
, including scope, change orders, commercial risk, and contract compliance.
Strong scheduling and project controls experience
on complex construction programs.
Experience managing large projects in the $50M–$100M+ range
.
Extensive experience in electrical utility construction, preferably high-voltage transmission
.
765kV experience is highly preferred
, although candidates with significant 345kV–500kV transmission construction experience
will be considered.
Proven ability to manage large project teams and work effectively with both field operations and executive leadership.
Strong understanding of construction productivity, manpower planning, equipment utilization, procurement, cost controls, and project execution.
Excellent leadership, communication, commercial, and problem-solving capabilities.

Ideal Candidate Profile The target candidate is a high-performing Director-level utility construction leader
who has grown through project and operational management roles on the contractor side of the industry.
They should understand not only how utilities operate, but more importantly how a contractor successfully executes and makes money on large utility construction projects
. This includes direct experience with P&L ownership, contracts, scheduling, project controls, PMO processes, field execution, and client management.
The successful candidate does not necessarily need to be a current VP or senior executive. The focus is on finding someone with the right hands-on operational depth and large-project experience
who is ready to take ownership of a highly visible transmission program.

Travel & Location The position will be based in Fort Worth, Texas
, with travel approximately three days per week
to project locations throughout Texas, including the Odessa, Abilene, and Killeen areas
.
A company truck will be provided
, and the successful candidate will participate in the company's Management by Objectives (MBO) incentive program
.

Job Title: Design & Development Director (15-Month FTC)

Location: Norfolk / Hybrid

Reporting To: Chief Product Officer

Who We Are

At Monica Vinader, we believe luxury should be empowering, long-lasting and responsibly made. Guided by integrity, craftsmanship and innovation, our goal is to elevate people’s lives by opening access to a more beautiful world.

From crafting consciously with recycled precious metals and ethically sourced materials, to designing enduring, versatile pieces made to be layered, loved and lived in every day, we are redefining what modern jewellery can be. We create jewellery that marks moments, tells stories and becomes part of who you are, all while making responsible luxury more accessible.

Our Commitment To Sustainability, Innovation And Positive Impact Continues To Be Recognised Across The Industry. We Are Proud To Have Received

Responsible Jewellery Brand, 2026 – Country & Town House
Responsible Luxury Business of the Year, 2025 & 2026 – Positive Luxury
Top 50 Inspiring Workplaces (UK & NI), 2024 – Inspiring Workplaces

With a global footprint across physical retail, e-commerce and trusted partners, we put our community at the heart of everything we do. Proudly female-founded and inclusive, we build meaningful relationships with the people who wear and love our jewellery.

Where we need your help

The Design & Development Director leads Monica Vinader's Design & Development function and drives our creative pipeline from brief through to development sign off — the guardian of the brief, the driver of the calendar, and the person who ensures creative delivery meets our standards and pace.

We need someone with a genuinely strong point of view: someone who will sit in a critique and say clearly whether the work answers the brief, is new enough, and will sell — and hold that line with the design team, the founder and the ELT.

This is a 15 month fixed term contract with a defined mandate: land creative direction and product pipeline for FY27 and FY28 against agreed go-to-market and critical path milestones, leading a team of three direct reports covering design and product development. You will report to the Chief Product Officer.

Your time spans briefing, critique, creative planning, critical path oversight, team leadership and cross-functional work with Merchandising, Supply, Brand & Regions — a role that is detailed as well as strategic; you'll be as comfortable in a technical pack as in a boardroom.

This role requires 2-3 days per week at our Holkham (Norfolk) office, with hybrid working for the remainder, or the London office where that suits.

What You’ll Do

Role Purpose

The Design & Development Director is accountable for the brief, the plan, the commerciality and the on time delivery of Monica Vinader's design and development output. You write and own the brief, working tightly with the category team, you own the creative calendar, you chair critique, you judge the work against the brief, you drive decisions to a conclusion, and you hold the Design & Development team to the go to market and critical path calendar.

You are the single point of accountability for whether the brief is met, whether the work is developable, and when it lands. Operating in a fast paced, agile environment, you will balance granular detail with strategic thinking to drive a consistent, innovative product pipeline.

Guardian of the Brief (Accountable)

Co-create the brief: With our Head of Category Management, write and own the design brief for every project and season, so there is a single, unambiguous statement of what the work must achieve: customer, occasion, price architecture, category need, margin, volume, option count and what "new" means in this context.
Judge against the brief & hold the line: Assess every concept presented against the brief and say so clearly, in the room, with reasons. Your judgement is on brief compliance, newness, customer relevance and commerciality.
Delivery to the brief: As concepts evolve, ensure alignment to the brief, or validate deviation from the brief is for a strategic region. Own this clarity and decision making. Ensure there is strong tension between the brand, regional and commercial needs vs creative innovation and distinctiveness, and this is aligned and resolved appropriately.

Creative Strategy & Planning

Creative plan & direction: own the seasonal creative plan sequenced against go-to-market milestones; facilitate agreement on seasonal direction between the CPO and Co-Founder & Artistic Director, converting it into actionable briefs.
Design language: Hold the team to the Monica Vinader design language across proportion, finish, construction, layering and wearability, using the Co-Founder & Artistic Director and Senior Designer as the reference point, so every piece is recognisably MV. You will apply and defend a standard you did not personally set
Commercial brief: Respond to the annual Product Brief and seasonal commercial briefs with viable design options against price architecture, category need, margin and volume expectations
Trends & aesthetic benchmarking: Ensure trend, material and competitor benchmarking happens to a defined cadence, is properly briefed into the team, and converts into design opportunities that land in the seasonal plan
Originality & IP: Own originality assessment at concept stage, and the IP and design registration gates

Briefing, Critique & Design Process

Design exploration: Ensure multiple routes are explored against every brief and properly finessed before a supplier is briefed
Critique & sign off: Own the design calendar and chair critique. Give a clear view, drive to a decision rather than another round, record it. You sign off that the brief is met and the work can enter development
Supplier briefing & cost: Own that supplier briefs are complete and on time, with technical content authored by the Head of Product Development. Hold the team to cost targets at concept stage, and champion component reuse to cut cost, lead time and complexity

Development Milestones & Critical Path (Accountable)

Critical path & sample approval: hold accountability for development milestones against the critical path (delivery led by the Head of Product Development)
Viability, quality & escalation: ensure designs are viable, manufacturable and meet quality standards; use returns/repairs insight to design out known failure modes; surface slippage, cost or quality risk to the CPO early, with options to solve.
Process ownership: own and continuously improve the NPD process end to end, including gate definitions and the calendar of alignment moments between Design, Merchandising, Supply and Brand.

Design & Development Team Leadership

Lead the team: lead, coach and develop three direct reports (product development, senior design, junior design), setting clear objectives and giving direct feedback. Lead creative specialists without being their creative author — your authority comes from clarity, judgement and advocacy, not out-designing them.
Learn the craft: get fluent in MV's materials, constructions and manufacturing constraints quickly, so you can support the team in the detail, not just manage it.
Resourcing & founder mentorship: structure workload against the product plan, flagging resourcing risk early; support the founder-led mentorship the Co-Founder & Artistic Director gives the design team.
Fixed-term handover: document process, decisions and design intent throughout the contract, and develop the team so the function is fully transferable at handover — holding the team steady through the period of transition.

Cross-Functional Leadership & Integration

Brand, Merchandising, Supply: partner with Brand on consistent product storytelling; with Merchandising/Category on assortment architecture and range rationalisation; with Supply & Quality on cost, capacity and sourcing decisions, engaging early so supplier capability shapes the range as it's built.
Sustainability, trade & trading forums: design within MV's responsible sourcing commitments; support trade, wholesale and regional requirements; represent Design & Development in range review and go-to-market forums, defending decisions with commercial reasoning.
Presentation & ambassadorship: own the Seasonal Product Presentation and timely issue of design assets; represent Design & Development to the ELT, the wider business, and independently on supplier visits and sourcing trips; keep the design studio a functional, inspirational creative space.

What You’ll Bring

Category background: A jewellery background is not required — we're open to leaders from adjacent design-led categories (fashion, accessories, footwear, watches, eyewear, leather goods, homeware, beauty, premium consumer product), provided you've driven a design and development pipeline at pace and with rigour, and can build technical fluency quickly.
Point of view: A clear, expressible point of view on customer, commerciality, newness and process one you'll voice in the room, defend under challenge from senior stakeholders including the founder and CPO, and commit to fully once a decision is made.
Calendar ownership: Proven end-to-end ownership of a product calendar (brief → concept → development → sign off → launch), holding a Head of Product Development to account without being the deepest technical expert in the room.
Organisation: Exceptional organisation across complex, multi-workstream calendars with many dependencies — evidence of building or fixing a critical path, not just working to one.
Range of altitude: Comfortable operating strategically and in the detail of a range plan, critical path or technical pack — this is a small, fast team.
Leadership of creative people: A track record of leading designers or other creative specialists and demonstrably improving their output.

Capability Framework Alignment

Applies Knowledge with Impact: Connects design decisions to margin, sell-through and customer relevance; anticipates cost, supply and quality risk at concept stage.
Communicates Effectively: Translates ambiguous or open creative input into clear, actionable briefs.
Coaches & Develops Others: Creates a development culture with direct, specific feedback.
Challenges & Commits: Leads constructive challenge on creative direction, then commits fully and unifies the team.
Embraces Change: Reframes ambiguity as opportunity and pivots priorities without losing momentum.

To be successful at Monica Vinader, it helps if you...

Are hands-on, solutions-focused, and entrepreneurial
Collaborate openly with humility, honesty, and humour
Embrace learning, teaching, and personal growth
Stay resilient, adaptable, and self-motivated in a creative environment
Speak up when you don’t know—and act fast to figure it out

Additional Requirements

Ability to document your authorisation to work in the United Kingdom.

Travel Requirements

This role requires 2-3 days in our Norfolk office. Outside of this, hybrid working is an option or being based in the London office.

Regular travel oversees (Italy, India, Thailand) 1-2 times per year

Our Aims and Values

Our mission is to be the leading accessible luxury brand, by delivering outstanding quality, design and customer service. We are:

Customer Obsessed

We put our customers at the centre of every decision and deliver thoughtful, personal experiences.

Caring

We act with respect and empathy for people, communities, and the planet.

Fast Paced

We move with focus and flexibility to make progress quickly and decisively.

Exceptional

We hold ourselves to high standards and are always learning, improving, and raising the bar.

Commercial

We make smart, data-led decisions that create long-term value for the business and our customers.

Monica Vinader as a global business makes the following inclusive culture pledge:

Our jewellery is for everyone and so is our community. Together, we will continue to implement sustainable changes to ensure that

jobs.title: Executive Director, Product Lifecycle & Membership Marketing
jobs.description:
Why USAA?

At USAA, our mission is to empower our members to achieve financial security through highly competitive products, exceptional service and trusted advice. We seek to be the #1 choice for the military community and their families.

Embrace a fulfilling career at USAA, where our core values – honesty, integrity, loyalty and service – define how we treat each other and our members. Be part of what truly makes us special and impactful.

We are proud to support active-duty military spouses. USAA roles may offer remote or hybrid flexibility for active-duty military spouses consistent with applicable policy and business needs.

The Opportunity

As Executive Director, Product Lifecycle & Membership Marketing, you will lead product marketers to acquire new accounts, shape and implement product-specific marketing strategies, focus on performance metrics, and deliver measurable results. You will accelerate growth through continuous test-and-learn agenda, improvement of paid marketing efforts, and expert allocation of marketing investments. Your team will ideate, plan, launch, measure, and optimize marketing campaigns to drive sustainable growth at efficient Cost Per Account (CPAs). You will be accountable for a large marketing budget, and you will collaborate closely with internal stakeholders such as Brand, Product, Risk, and Analytics to drive growth via both new-to-USAA members as well as cross-selling to existing members. Strong analytical skills, business acumen, and entrepreneurial spirit are key to success in this role.

We offer a flexible work environment that requires an individual to be in the office 4 days per week.
This position can be based in one of the following locations: San Antonio, TX, Plano, TX, Phoenix, AZ, Colorado Springs, CO, Charlotte, NC, or Tampa, FL (Chesapeake, VA – Property and Casualty roles ONLY). Relocation assistance is available for this position.

What You'll Do

Responsible for fully digital-first marketing lifecycle, inclusive of strategy, member research, planning, direct response marketing, agency management, creative development, compliant execution, analytics and optimization, and performance management for a subset of products that they support.
Develop and implement marketing plans and campaigns to build and deepen USAA's relationship with existing members, and drive acquisition of new members.
Manage multiple product marketing budgets to deliver sustainable growth at efficient Cost per Account (CPAs) at scale.
Accountable for digital acquisition experience, lead adoption of new ways of working, and leverage storytelling to drive understanding & adoption of change.
Adopt & lead a team to embrace safe & sound business practices at scale.
Provide thought leadership within and keen awareness of the external digital space, with established network of external partners to inspire out-of-box thinking.
Significant knowledge in product related regulations, and risk and compliance requirements.
Thrive working with cross-functional teams. Effective change agent that can get the job done and push mission forward while managing multiple stakeholder interests and expectations along the way.
Keep USAA brand and our mission to serve the military community at the forefront of new marketing practice.
Attract, develop, expand, and retain high performing teams of marketing professionals that deliver outcomes and key results.
Cultivate talent through coaching and training.
Ensures risks associated with business activities are effectively identified, measured, monitored, and controlled in accordance with risk and compliance policies and procedures.

Education

Bachelor's degree; OR 4 years of relevant education and/or experience. MBA preferred.

What You Have

10+ years of relevant work experience in financial services with hands-on marketing experience in conversion channels (i.e. Paid Search, Affiliates, Direct Mail).
4+ years of people leadership experience in building, managing and/or developing high-performing teams required.
Experience collaborating with key resources and stakeholders, influencing decisions, and managing work to achieve strategic goals required.
Executive-level business acumen in the areas of business operations, industry practices and emerging trends required.
Demonstrated ability to create and articulate a vision for product marketing organization.
Ability to seek and analyze data from variety of resources to support marketing decisions and alignment with key stakeholders.
Demonstrated proficiency in Product Marketing, including setting growth objectives, developing marketing plans, performance reporting, and driving incremental growth consumer definition, situation assessment, financial analysis, and marketing strategy.
Demonstrated proficiency in marketing data analytics.
Excellent communication skills (verbal and written) with the ability to adjust communication style based on the audiences.
Strong analytical skills with the ability to analyze and evaluate information.
Ability to exercise appropriate judgment by using information and knowledge to make timely, effective decisions.
Ability to adjust scope or resources as appropriate, mitigating potential risk to projects.

What Sets You Apart

5+ years of Property & Casualty product marketing experience, with a focus on auto insurance acquisition. Proven success driving growth in a direct-to-consumer model across offline and digital channels, including Paid Search, Affiliates, and Direct Mail.
Demonstrated expertise in direct-to-consumer product marketing, including growth planning, marketing strategy, performance measurement, financial analysis, and data-driven decision making.
Demonstrated expertise in audience strategy and lifecycle marketing, including audience definition, segmentation, personalization, and engagement strategies that drive customer acquisition, deepening, retention, and lifetime value.
Hands-on experience with Salesforce and modern marketing automation, personalization, and customer data platforms.
Deep understanding of the P&C insurance business and financial drivers, with the ability to connect marketing investments and strategies to portfolio performance, profitability, growth objectives, and P&L outcomes.
Exceptional communication, influence, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to build alignment across a complex matrixed organization and effectively engage senior leaders and cross-functional partners.
Proven ability to build strong marketing partnerships, align audience strategies, optimize customer journeys, and deliver integrated programs that drive measurable business outcomes.
Strong analytical and strategic thinking skills, with the ability to translate complex data and market insights into actionable recommendations and executive-level decisions, particularly within the P&C market.
Experience working in and/or leading cross-functional agile teams, serving as a team lead or product owner, and setting priorities and strategic direction.
US military experience through military service or a military spouse/domestic partner.

Compensation range: The salary range for this position is: $169,880.00 - $305,780.00

USAA does not provide visa sponsorship for this role. Please do not apply for this role if at any time (now or in the future) you will need immigration support (i.e., H-1B, TN, STEM OPT Training Plans, etc.).

Compensation:
USAA has an effective process for assessing market data and establishing ranges to ensure we remain competitive. You are paid within the salary range based on your experience and market data of the position.

Employees may be eligible for pay incentives based on overall corporate and individual performance and at the discretion of the USAA Board of Directors.

The above description reflects the details considered necessary to describe the principal functions of the job and should not be construed as a detailed description of all the work requirements that may be performed in the job.

Long Term Incentive Plan: Cash payment for Executive level roles only, representing a cash payment which is both time and performance based.

Benefits:
At USAA our employees enjoy best-in-class benefits to support their physical, financial, and emotional wellness. These benefits include comprehensive medical, dental and vision plans, 401(k), pension, life insurance, parental benefits, adoption assistance, paid time off program with paid holidays plus 16 paid volunteer hours, and various wellness programs. Additionally, our career path planning and continuing education assists employees with their professional goals.

For more details on our outstanding benefits, visit our benefits page on USAAjobs.com.

Applications for this position are accepted on an ongoing basis, this posting will remain open until the position is filled. Thus, interested candidates are encouraged to apply the same day they view this posting.

USAA is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or status as a protected veteran.

new_jobs.description:
Company Description
Guisados is a 10 unit restaurant brand headquartered in Los Angeles, California. The family owned restaurant continues to serve its famous homestyle braises on handmade tortillas since 2010 with over 175 employees across 10 restaurants with a commissary style operation. With locations in Boyle Heights, Echo Park, DTLA, Hermosa Beach, West Hollywood, Venice, Long Beach, Pasadena, Burbank and Beverly Hills Guisados continues to pride itself on quality, afforable and authentic food with service at its core.

Role Description
The Chief Operating Officer (COO) is a full-time, on-site role based in Los Angeles, CA. Responsible for overseeing day-to-day operations and ensuring organizational effectiveness. This role includes leading operational planning, coordinating cross-functional activities, and implementing processes that support business goals and client delivery. The COO will work closely with senior leadership to manage budgets, monitor financial performance, and optimize resource allocation. Daily tasks involve assessing operational risks, analyzing performance metrics, refining workflows, and supporting staff to maintain high-quality marketing and advertising services.

● Operational Excellence - Implement and optimize operational processes and procedures to ensure efficiency and cost-effectiveness. Continuously improve supply chain, inventory management, and logistics to meet customer demands.
● Customer Service – Ensure that the highest level of customer service is performed at each café. Implement a comprehensive training program to ensure that each team member has the skill set to provide exceptional customer service.
● Project Management - Lead and oversee complex projects related to expansion, store renovations, and process improvements. Develop project plans, set timelines, allocate resources, and ensure successful project delivery.
● Training/ Onboarding - Creating training guides and day to day to-dos for every role across all departments.
● Human Resources and Leadership Development - Oversee the HR function, including recruitment, talent management, and employee development. Develop and implement leadership training programs to cultivate a high-performing and engaged workforce.
● Financial Management - Monitor financial performance, budgets, and key performance indicators to ensure profitability and cost control. Analyze financial data to make informed decisions and recommendations.
● Team Management - Build and lead a high-performing team of leaders, ensuring alignment with the company's goals and values. Foster a positive and inclusive work environment, promoting collaboration and innovation.
● Future Growth - create framework for future expansion into new markets. From training guides to store level plug and play roadmaps for opening new locations in the future, this persons role is not ONLY maintain the status quo of todays Guisados; but to help create a future into new and developing opportunities across southern California (and beyond).

Qualifications

● Minimum of 10 years’ experience in a complex operational environment, with progressively increasing responsibilities.
● Bilingual and proficient in both english and spanish language
● Proven experience in multi-unit retail operations is highly desirable.
● Strong leadership and people management skills, with a track record of building and developing high-performing teams.
● Exceptional critical thinking and problem-solving abilities.
● Proficiency in project management methodologies and tools.
● Knowledge of Human Resources and talent development practices.
● Financial acumen and experience in managing budgets and resources.
● Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
● Responsibility for the customer service program at a retail company.
● Bachelor's degree in business administration, management, or a related field (MBA preferred).

new_jobs.title: Managing Director
new_jobs.description:
Who is Trace3
?
Trace3 is a leading Transformative IT Authority, providing unique technology solutions and consulting services to our clients. Equipped with elite engineering and dynamic innovation, we empower IT executives and their organizations to achieve competitive advantage through a process of Integrate, Automate, Innovate.
Our culture at Trace3 embodies the spirit of a startup with the advantage of a scalable business. Employees can grow their career and have fun while doing it!
Trace3 is headquartered in Irvine, California. We employ more than 1,200 people all over the United States. Our major field office locations include Denver, Indianapolis, Grand Rapids, Lexington, Los Angeles, Louisville, Texas, San Francisco.  
Ready to discover the possibilities that live in technology?

Come Join Us!

Street-Smart
  -  Thriving in Dynamic Times

We are flexible and resilient in a fast-changing environment. We continuously innovate and drive constructive change while keeping a focus on the “big picture.” We exercise sound business judgment in making high-quality decisions in a timely and cost-effective manner. We are highly creative and can dig deep within ourselves to find positive solutions to different problems.
Juice -  The “Stuff” it takes to be a Needle Mover

We get things done and drive results. We lead without a title, empowering others through a can-do attitude. We look forward to the goal, mentally mapping out every checkpoint on the pathway to success, and visualizing what the final destination looks and feels like.
Teamwork -  Humble, Hungry and Smart

We are humble individuals who understand how our job impacts the company's mission. We treat others with respect, admit mistakes, give credit where it’s due and demonstrate transparency. We “bring the weather” by exhibiting positive leadership and solution-focused thinking. We hug people in their trials, struggles, and failures – not just their success. We appreciate the individuality of the people around us.

JOB SUMMARY:

  Under the direction of the General Manager and Account Executive, the Managing Director leads consultative campaigns across products and services within the Security, Cloud, and Data domains—from contract signature through delivery—ensuring scope, deliverables, budget, client satisfaction, and business outcomes are met. This role supports the full project lifecycle (presales through delivery) to confirm solutions are properly scoped, designed, implemented, and tested to meet client needs. This is not an account management role; the position reports directly to the Account Executive(s) for the accounts served.  
SUMMARY OF ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS:

  Stakeholder Management & Engagement

Build trusted relationships with senior leaders, project sponsors, and business units to understand objectives and priorities.  

Serve as the primary point of contact between business units and technical teams to align goals and solutions.  

Define success metrics with stakeholders for strategic initiatives and sales targets.  

Sales Strategy & Revenue Growth

Develop and execute sales strategies to identify and pursue opportunities, win new business, and expand existing accounts.  

Upsell and cross-sell by recommending products, services, and solutions aligned to customer goals.  

Build, maintain, and forecast an accurate sales pipeline from prospecting through close.  

Lead contract negotiations and pricing discussions to secure new business while aligning to client needs and profitability goals, in collaboration with the Account Manager.  

Manage the partner agreement process with Trace3.  

Review current agreements (as applicable).  

If additional agreements are needed, engage the appropriate Trace3 team to initiate the process.  

Serve as the liaison between Trace3 and partners, coordinating action items through execution.  

Engagement oversight  

Oversee project delivery to ensure client and stakeholder satisfaction.  

Drive timely partner resource assignment.  

Review and process change orders internally (as applicable).  

Strategic Planning & Roadmap Development

Partner with domain leaders to create and execute short- and long-term strategies aligned to sales and business goals.  

Develop networking and collaboration roadmaps with milestones, timelines, and revenue targets.  

Align technology and sales efforts to ensure offerings meet business needs and generate revenue.  

Project Leadership & Oversight

Own execution of strategic projects to keep work on track and deliver measurable outcomes.  

Coordinate with project managers, engineering, and sales to deliver solutions that meet business and revenue goals.  

Identify and mitigate risks to project execution and sales success.  

Sales Performance Monitoring & Reporting

Monitor and report on sales metrics (revenue growth, performance, and market penetration) and provide actionable insights to leadership.  

Prepare client proposals, progress reports, and sales forecasts for clients and senior stakeholders.  

Meet or exceed sales quotas and KPIs for engagement and revenue growth.  

Networking and Collaboration Advocacy & Communication

Advocate for networking and collaboration needs internally and externally, ensuring domain priorities are reflected in product, sales, and resourcing decisions.  

Provide regular updates on project delivery and sales performance, including market opportunities and customer feedback.  

Cross-functional Collaboration

Work with sales, marketing, product management, engineering, and customer success to support strategic projects and sales opportunities.  

Align cross-functional efforts to support domain initiatives and meet technical and sales objectives.  

Escalate sales or technical issues as needed and drive cross-team resolution.  

Daily Tasks:  
Sales Strategy & Client Prospecting (30%)  

Identify sales opportunities within the domain and develop tailored pursuit strategies, including new-client prospecting.  

Stakeholder + Partner/Vendor Engagement & Relationship Building (25%)  

Meet with stakeholders, vendors, and partners to align strategic priorities and sales targets and maintain senior-leader relationships.  

Project Oversight & Sales Pipeline Management (20%)  

Manage technical projects and sales opportunities, ensuring alignment with client needs and business objectives.  

Reporting & Data Analysis (15%)  

Prepare and present sales forecasts, performance metrics, and project status reports.  

Cross-Functional Collaboration (10%)  

Partner with internal teams to deliver projects on time and support sales opportunities.  

REQUIRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

new_jobs.title: Director of Advancement
new_jobs.description:
Help Shape the Future of a Pioneering Community

CBST is seeking a strategic, creative, and relationship-driven Director of Advancement
to help lead the next chapter of our vibrant, progressive Jewish community.

CBST is an LGBTQ+ synagogue rooted in inclusivity, equity, and radical welcome. We welcome people of all sexual orientations, gender identities, family structures, racial and ethnic backgrounds, and Jewish journeys. Grounded in Jewish tradition and committed to justice, learning, and spiritual exploration, CBST is a place where people come to build community, find meaning, and work toward a more just world.

Reporting to the Executive Director, the Director of Advancement will be a senior member of CBST's leadership team, working closely with our Co-Clergy leads, staff, the Board of Directors, and lay leaders.

This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced advancement professional who is energized by building relationships, telling compelling stories, growing communities, and helping an extraordinary institution thrive.

The Opportunity

The Director of Advancement will provide strategic leadership across fundraising, membership, communications, marketing, stewardship, and community engagement
.

You will lead CBST's efforts to grow philanthropic support, strengthen and retain membership, deepen relationships with donors and congregants, and increase CBST's visibility and impact.

Key areas of responsibility include:

Spearheading CBST's annual fundraising, major gifts, planned giving, grants, and special campaigns, including but not limited to: fundraising events, donor cultivation opportunities, Pride initiatives, and other special programs.
Managing and growing relationships with major donors and building a strong pipeline of future supporters.
Expanding membership recruitment, engagement, stewardship, and retention.
Developing an integrated advancement strategy, including annual goals, plans, calendars, and budgets.
Driving marketing, communications, and institutional storytelling that bring CBST's mission and impact to life.
Partnering with the Executive Director and Senior Co-Clergy on public messaging and communications related to issues central to CBST and its community.
Strengthening CBST's brand and presence throughout New York City's Jewish, LGBTQ+, philanthropic, and broader civic communities.
Fostering relationships with donors and members by bringing together clergy, staff, Board members, and lay leaders in coordinated stewardship and engagement efforts. 
Providing strategic oversight of advancement systems and data to support strong decision-making, effective relationship management, and long-term growth.
Guiding and supporting the Manager of Development Operations, Membership & Engagement Manager, and Communications Coordinator.

Who You Are

You are a strategic and entrepreneurial relationship-builder who enjoys connecting people to a mission they care about. You can see the big picture while also moving important work forward. You are comfortable working with donors, clergy, Board members, volunteers, and staff—and you understand that successful advancement is ultimately about building authentic, lasting relationships.

We are looking for someone with:

At least five years of progressively responsible nonprofit fundraising or advancement experience.
Demonstrated success in annual giving, major gifts, planned giving, grants, and donor stewardship.
Experience with membership-based organizations, community engagement, marketing, and/or communications.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills and a gift for compelling storytelling.
Strong strategic thinking, organizational, project-management, and relationship-building skills.
Experience with CRM or fundraising databases; Salesforce experience is strongly preferred.
A commitment to creating inclusive, affirming spaces that honor LGBTQ+ people and diverse identities.
Familiarity with Jewish traditions and communal life—or a genuine openness and enthusiasm for learning.

Why CBST?

CBST offers the opportunity to do meaningful work at the intersection of Jewish life, LGBTQ+ community, justice, spirituality, and social change
. You will join a collaborative, mission-driven team and help shape the future of one of New York City's most distinctive Jewish communities.
We offer a comprehensive and competitive benefits package, generous paid time off, opportunities for professional development and Jewish learning, and a hybrid work environment. 
Salary range is $120k-$140K annually and is commensurate with experience. 

To Apply

Please email a resume and cover letter to Carrie Connor, Executive Director
, at careers@cbst.org with “Director of Advancement”
in the subject line. Tell us why this opportunity interests you and how your experience and perspective would contribute to CBST.

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis.

CBST is committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. People of all backgrounds—especially LGBTQ+ individuals, Jews of Color, people with disabilities, and individuals from historically underrepresented communities—are strongly encouraged to apply.

Provide strategic direction and operational oversight for the Office of Equity and the Title IX and Civil Rights Compliance unit. The Executive Director will also lead the Civil Rights and Title IX office and is responsible for overseeing compliance with civil rights and equal employment opportunity laws, regulations and policies related to race, ethnicity, color, creed, religion, national origin, citizenship or immigration status, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, age, genetic status, marital status, disability, veteran or military status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local law. 60% - Administer and oversee the University’s Equal Opportunity policies and procedures in all aspects of employment and education, ensuring compliance across the University with federal and state civil rights and equal employment opportunity laws and regulations, including Titles VI and VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, Title IX of the Education Amendments of 1972, the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), and the Washington Law Against Discrimination.

Provide technical guidance to the university about obligations under the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) and grievance procedures for individuals who experience discrimination on the basis of disability. Mediate and resolve disputes that arise as a result of the implementation of ADA accommodations.

10% - Lead CRTC Office

Oversee office personnel and budget. Maintain office climate of inclusion, integrity, impartiality, and care for staff and clients. Represent the unit and/or the University on committees, task forces, and other local and state bodies.

Required Qualifications

JD and a minimum of (8) years of progressive experience addressing the legal, education, administrative and/or management responsibilities of a university, or an equivalent combination of education and professional work experience.
Administrative experience in higher education.
Advanced knowledge and experience interpreting and applying civil rights, equal employment opportunity, and Title IX laws and regulations.
Experience leading trauma-informed and culturally appropriate investigations
Knowledge of higher education policies and practices and experience in promoting principles and practices of diversity, equity, and inclusion.
Understanding of, sensitivity to, and respect for the diverse academic, socio-economic, racial, ethnic, religious, and cultural backgrounds, disabilities, gender identities, and sexual orientations of students, faculty, and staff.

Excellent project and time management skills.
Flexibility, adaptability, and capacity to work in a dynamic work environment.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience working within collective bargaining environments and shared governance structures.

The Managing Director of Finance is a senior financial leadership opportunity with broad influence across OHSU Foundation. Reporting to the CFO – VP of Finance & Administration, this leader will help shape and implement financial strategy while overseeing critical areas including financial reporting, fund and endowment accounting, trust administration, internal controls, audit, and financial policy.

Just as importantly, this is a highly collaborative role. Design, implement, and monitor internal controls over financial reporting while protecting the integrity of the Foundation's financial reporting systems.
Evaluate and evolve accounting and reporting practices as contributions, funds under management, regulatory requirements, and gift complexity continue to grow.
Partner with key OHSU faculty and finance leaders to provide strategic financial guidance and support the effective use of Foundation gift funds.
Trust Administration & Endowment Accounting – 30%:
Develop and implement approaches to assess and manage risk associated with charitable gift annuity agreements and provide regular updates to the Investment Committee.
Collaborate with gift planning colleagues to optimize trust and annuity administration.
Donor Strategy & Stewardship – 20%:

Evaluate unusual assets and complex gift scenarios and provide thoughtful financial recommendations.
Help translate Board-approved financial and investment policy into effective operating practices across the organization.

Master's degree in accounting, finance, business administration, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
10+ years of broad experience across investment, tax, and general accounting.
Demonstrated expertise in generally accepted accounting principles, nonprofit accounting, investment and endowment accounting, tax reporting, and financial reporting systems.
Strong understanding of investment concepts, practices, and procedures.
Experience managing and assessing financial and business risk and developing appropriate recommendations.
Exceptional analytical skills, including the ability to locate, model, interpret, and communicate complex financial information from multiple sources.

Ability to effectively advise and collaborate with senior leadership, staff, trustees, faculty partners, and external constituents.
Strong communication and influencing skills with the ability to make complex financial concepts accessible to varied audiences.

ROLE TITLE: Managing Director, Account Management, National Corporate Partnerships
(Full-time)

POSITION REPORTS TO: Jerry Ochoa, Vice President, National Corporate Partnerships

PRIORITY APPLICATION DEADLINE: Sep 1, 2026 at 11:59PM ET

LOCATION: Flexible

What You'll Do

We are looking for a Managing Director, Account Management to lead Teach For America's national corporate account management portfolio and drive the retention, deepening, and expansion of our current corporate partnerships. In this role, you will set the vision, strategy, and stewardship approach that keep our most important corporate partners closely engaged with TFA's mission, and you will personally manage a portfolio of six- and seven-figure partners. While net-new corporate partner acquisition sits with the MD, Business Development, this role owns the expansion and upsell of existing partnerships — including converting current partners into larger, multi-year, and transformational investors.

The ideal candidate will be passionate about building durable, mission-aligned partnerships with senior corporate leaders and translating those relationships into sustained, multi-year investments. You bring a best-in-class customer service orientation, a rigorous attention to detail, strong strategic thinking, and the ability to take a bird's-eye view of the portfolio while attending to any and all needs of each corporate partner. You bring curiosity and openness to how emerging technologies — particularly AI — can accelerate your work, and you approach these tools with fluency, critical thinking, and a strong ethical grounding.

The goal for this role in particular is to retain and grow TFA's existing corporate revenue base by delivering exceptional partner experiences that convert current partners into long-term, transformational investors.

What You'll Be Responsible For

Portfolio Strategy and Vision (20%)

Set the annual and multi-year strategy for the corporate account management portfolio, including national and nationally-managed revenue goals.
Develop annual priorities and tactics designed to retain, deepen, and grow current corporate partners.
Build and maintain the account management team's infrastructure, KPIs, and workflow management processes.

Portfolio Management and Partner Stewardship (40%)

Lead a portfolio of six- and seven-figure corporate partners at the national and regional levels.
Serve as primary strategist and central relationship manager for TFA's current corporate partners.
Serve as the primary external representative of TFA with current corporate donors, including engagement with C-suite leaders, corporate foundation executives, and CSR/ESG heads.
Oversee, strategize, and/or execute on general fundraising operations and stewardship of corporate funders, including renewals, impact reporting, and recognition.
Ensure newly closed partners are successfully transitioned from the Business Development sub-team, delivering a best-in-class donor experience across the partnership lifecycle.

Cross-Functional Collaboration and Enterprise Development (15%)

Forge and foster deep partnerships with regional fundraising teams and national colleagues to build mutually beneficial engagement strategies that meet partner priorities and TFA's priorities.
Leverage TFA's network of national and regional board members, senior leaders, and program teams to retain and grow current partners.
Contribute to enterprise-wide development mindsets and donor-centered strategies across TFA.
Lead complex, cross-functional project management to deliver on partnership commitments — managing down, across, and up within the organization and with external partners.
Explore, develop, and responsibly apply AI tools to strengthen partner stewardship, portfolio management, and internal workflows — modeling curious, ethical, and critically-minded use of emerging technology for the sub-team and the broader NCPT.

People Management and Team Culture (15%)

Manage and develop your direct report (for our current fiscal year this will likely mean managing one Director on the Account Management sub-team) toward their annual retention and growth goals.
Onboard, coach, and empower direct reports to grow as professional fundraisers and to meet their portfolio and revenue targets.
Build an equitable and inclusive sub-team culture within Account Management that reflects TFA's core values.
Support the professional growth and long-term trajectory of direct reports.

Contribution to Team, Development, and Organizational Culture (10%)

Contribute to a collective culture of excellence, teamwork, Core Values leadership, and commitment to DEI on the NCPT, National Development Team, and across the organization.
Participate in special projects (e.g., economic model sprints, cross-team initiatives such as the Lead Now Fund).
Step into leadership and facilitation opportunities at the Development team and organization level.
Speak with respect and courage when necessary to improve processes, culture, and mindsets aligned to TFA's Foundations and Core Values.

A WEEK IN THE LIFE

Over the course of any week, the Managing Director, Account Management will spend time:

Preparing for and leading stewardship, renewal, and growth conversations with senior executives at current corporate partners.
Coaching direct reports on portfolio strategy, partner communications, and renewal execution.
Building and refining impact reports, renewal proposals, and other high-stakes partner-facing materials.
Experimenting with and applying AI tools to accelerate research, drafting, analysis, and preparation — and sharing learnings with the team.
Partnering with the VP, NCPT and MD, Business Development to align on team goals, portfolio health, and cross-sub-team handoffs.
Collaborating with regional fundraising leaders on shared partners and cross-cutting opportunities.
Tracking portfolio activity, retention rates, and revenue projections in Salesforce and other reporting tools.
Representing TFA at partner-facing events, executive briefings, and stewardship convenings.

Your Experience

Your areas of knowledge and expertise that matter most for this role (minimum qualifications):

Ability to build and manage a high-performing corporate account management function, from strategy through execution.
Expertise in the corporate philanthropy, corporate social responsibility, and/or corporate partnerships landscape.
Strong strategic thinking, with the ability to identify opportunities to deepen and grow existing partnerships.
Proficient in senior-level relationship management, including engaging with C-suite executives and corporate foundation leaders.
Best-in-class customer service orientation and rigorous attention to detail.
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, including proposal writing, executive briefings, and impact reporting.
Rigorous project and portfolio management skills, with the ability to manage many complex partnerships simultaneously.
Strong people management skills and ability to develop direct reports.
Deep commitment to TFA's mission, values, and commitment to Diversity, Equity, and Inclusiveness.
Education: Bachelor's degree required.
Proficient in Microsoft Office; experience with Salesforce required.
Curiosity and openness to emerging technologies — including AI tools — with the fluency, critical thinking, and ethical grounding to explore, evaluate, and responsibly apply them in daily work.

BONUS (preferred Qualifications)

Prior Experience

At least 7 years of fundraising experience, partnership management, or account management experience with a strong track record of retaining and growing six- and seven-figure relationships.
Prior management experience, including managing to ambitious retention and revenue goals.
Experience in the education sector or in mission-driven nonprofit fundraising.
Experience navigating complex, national organizations with matrixed local and central teams.
CFRE (Certified Fund-Raising Executive) certification, MBA, or other advanced degree preferred.

Work Demands

Travel up to 3–4x per quarter for internal and external meetings.
Occasional evening and weekend work required to support high-stakes cultivation and stewardship activities.

Skills

Ability to take a bird's-eye view of the portfolio while attending to any and all details of each partner.
Ability to be entrepreneurial and flexible in a fast-paced, results-oriented culture.
Strong ability to influence others toward outcomes without direct authority.
Positive, can-do approach and ability to bring hopefulness and optimism to the team.
Prior experience integrating AI tools into fundraising, sales, communications, research, or knowledge management workflows.

YOUR FUTURE TEAM

The National Corporate Partnerships Team (NCPT) is one of five sub-teams on TFA's National Development Team. Our charge is to strengthen, grow, and create new corporate partnerships that maximize financial and broader contributions to TFA's mission and long-term sustainability. The Account Management sub-team is responsible for the retention, deepening, and expansion of TFA's existing corporate partner portfolio, working in close partnership with the Business Development sub-team, regional fundraisers, and enterprise-wide leaders. Under a five-person structure of VP + 2 MDs + 2 Directors, this MD will lead the Account Management function and directly shape TFA's most important, long-standing corporate relationships. NCPT is an AI-forward sub-team, actively exploring how emerging technology can deepen partner relationships, sharpen strategy, and expand our capacity — and we're looking for leaders who share that curiosity.

new_jobs.title: Chief Operating Officer
new_jobs.description:
Who We Are

Rowe Plastic Surgery (RPS)
is a multi-site aesthetic and reconstructive plastic surgery practice with locations in Montclair, NJ; Red Bank, NJ; New York (Park Avenue and 77th Street); and Palm Beach, FL. RPS is privately owned, with no board of directors, strategic and operating decisions are made in direct partnership with Ownership. RPS has built a strong regional reputation and a loyal patient base and is now entering its next phase of growth: professionalizing its infrastructure, scaling beyond a single-specialty model, and positioning the organization for institutional capital, joint venture partnerships, and/or a future transaction.

Position Summary

RPS is seeking a Chief Executive Officer
to be based in West Palm Beach Headquarters to lead the organization through its next stage of growth from an approximately 50-employee, founder-driven practice into a scaled, multi-platform healthcare organization. Reporting directly to Ownership, and partnering closely with the COO, VP of Human Resources, and Senior Financial Analyst, the CEO will serve as the senior-most operating executive of RPS, with full accountability for the organization in the absence of a formal board. The CEO will be responsible for both setting strategy and personally driving execution: building the operational backbone required to support growth, expanding RPS's service lines and market footprint beyond plastics and reconstructive surgery (including adjacent platforms such as IVF/fertility), and pursuing growth through joint ventures, M&A, and organic expansion. A core mandate of this role is to make RPS an attractive, well-run, and defensible platform for private equity investment or an eventual sale without sacrificing clinical quality, physician alignment, or patient experience along the way.

Core CEO Functions

Standard general-management responsibilities that come with sole executive accountability in a privately held company with no board:
•     Own overall P&L performance and financial results for the entire organization, across all sites and service lines.
•     Set organizational vision, mission, and long-term strategic direction in direct partnership with Ownership.
•     Serve as final decision-maker on major operational, financial, and strategic matters -sound independent judgment and clear communication with Ownership are essential.
•     Build, lead, and hold accountable the senior leadership team, including the COO, VP of HR, and Senior Financial Analyst, and define future executive hires (e.g., CFO) as the organization scales.
•     Ensure regulatory, legal, and clinical compliance across all sites and jurisdictions (NY, NJ, FL, GA).
•     Oversee financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, and internal controls, partnering closely with the Senior Financial Analyst (or future CFO)
•     Direct organizational design and talent strategy in partnership with the VP of HR, including workforce planning as RPS scales.
•     Own day-to-day operational performance in partnership with the COO, ensuring strategy translates into consistent execution at the site level.
•     Manage risk across the organization financial, operational, clinical, and reputational.
•     Represent RPS externally to physicians, patients, vendors, lenders, and potential investors or partners.
•     Allocate capital and resources across existing sites, new markets, and growth initiatives.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Strategy & Platform Growth

•     Develop and execute a multi-year growth strategy that scales RPS from its current single-specialty footprint into a diversified, multi-platform healthcare organization.
•     Identify and evaluate expansion into adjacent, complementary healthcare verticals (e.g., IVF/fertility, med spa, dermatology, wellness) that leverage RPS's brand, patient base, and referral relationships.
•     Define and prioritize new market entry, new geographies, new sites, and new service lines, based on demand, competitive dynamics, and return on investment.
•     Translate strategy into an actionable execution roadmap with clear milestones, ownership, and accountability, this is a builder/operator role, not a strategy-only mandate.

M&A, Joint Ventures & Capital Strategy

•     Lead sourcing, evaluation, negotiation, and integration of acquisition targets, joint ventures, and strategic partnerships that accelerate platform growth.
•     Understand and apply healthcare company valuation methodologies to assess acquisition targets, partnership structures, and RPS's own enterprise value over time.
•     Prepare RPS operationally and financially to be an attractive platform for private equity investment, recapitalization, or sale, including data room readiness, KPI infrastructure, and de-risking key-person dependencies.
•     Build and manage relationships with investment bankers, private equity sponsors, legal counsel, and other transaction advisors as RPS evaluates capital and exit options.
•     Design and execute go-to-market strategies for new service lines, locations, and partnerships, including positioning, channel strategy, and competitive differentiation.

Operational Leadership

•     In close partnership with the COO — not limited to financial projections and analysis but support the operational execution as required.
•     Partner closely with the COO, VP of HR, Senior Financial Analyst, clinical, and site leadership to ensure strategy translates into consistent execution at the practice level.
•     Establish and monitor KPIs and operating metrics across sites and service lines, driving accountability and continuous improvement.
•     Evaluate and implement technology, workflow, and process improvements that increase efficiency, patient experience, and margin as RPS scales.

Physician & Provider Compensation

•     Design, structure, and evolving physician and provider compensation models that align incentives with production, quality, patient experience, and organizational growth goals.
•     Benchmark physician compensation against market and specialty norms across plastics, reconstructive, and any newly added service lines.
•     Structure compensation approaches that support recruitment and retention of high-performing physicians while remaining sustainable and defensible in a future transaction or partnership.
•     Partner with HR and legal/compliance on physician contracts, productivity models, and equity or partnership structures where applicable.

Organizational Leadership & Culture

•     Build out an executive and operational leadership team capable of supporting a rapidly scaling, multi-site organization, including future roles (e.g., CFO) as RPS grows.
•     Partner with the VP of HR to formalize infrastructure — policies, compliance, talent, and culture — appropriate for a growth-stage healthcare platform.
•     Serve as the primary external face of RPS with investors, partners, physicians, and key stakeholders, while maintaining the culture and patient-first values that built the practice.
 QUALIFICATIONS

Required

•     10+ years of progressive healthcare leadership experience, including prior CEO, President, COO, or comparable executive-level operating role.
•     Direct experience scaling a healthcare services organization — ideally through a combination of organic growth, joint ventures, and M&A.
•     Strong operational background: demonstrated ability to build and run infrastructure, not solely to produce financial projections and analysis.
•     Working knowledge of company valuation methodologies and transaction dynamics relevant to private equity investment or sale of a healthcare platform.
•     Demonstrated experience developing and executing go-to-market strategy for new service lines, locations, or business units.
•     Experience designing physician or provider compensation structures, including productivity-based and hybrid models.
•     Proven ability to lead through ambiguity in a founder- or physician-led organization, balancing entrepreneurial speed with institutional rigor.

Preferred

•     Healthcare leadership experience within plastic surgery, aesthetics, or a closely related elective/specialty medical field.
•     Prior experience preparing a healthcare organization for private equity investment, recapitalization, or sale (platform or add-on experience).
•     Experience expanding a single-specialty healthcare business into adjacent verticals (e.g., fertility/IVF, medical aesthetics, wellness).
•     Existing network of relevant investment banking, private equity, and healthcare M&A relationships.
•     Advanced degree in Business, Healthcare Administration, or a related field (MBA, MHA, or equivalent experience).

What Success Look Like

•     A documented, Ownership-approved growth strategy with a clear roadmap for new markets, service lines, and/or acquisitions.
•     Operational infrastructure and KPI reporting in place across all sites, supporting scalable, repeatable growth.
•     At least one successfully evaluated or executed joint venture, acquisition, or new-platform launch within the first 18–24 months.
•     A physician compensation framework that is competitive, sustainable, and transaction-ready.
•     RPS positioned — financially and operationally — as a credible, attractive platform for private equity partnership or sale.

Rowe Plastic Surgery is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

Director of Development – School of Law

Are you a relationship-builder who thrives on connecting donor passions with transformational impact? The UND Alumni Association & Foundation is seeking a Director of Development to lead major gift fundraising efforts for the School of Law.

In this role, you'll partner closely with the Dean, faculty, and university leadership to identify, cultivate, and solicit major and planned gifts that advance the mission of the School of Law and the University of North Dakota. You'll manage a portfolio of high-capacity donors, develop meaningful engagement strategies, and inspire philanthropic investment through personalized outreach and compelling proposals.
We're looking for a motivated, strategic fundraiser who excels at building relationships, and communicating the value of higher education.

If you're ready to help shape the future of legal education through philanthropy, we'd love to hear from you.
POSITION SUMMARY
Reporting to the Vice President of Development, the Director of Development will work closely with the Dean of the School of Law and faculty to enhance and support their fundraising efforts. This position is primarily responsible for the qualification, cultivation and solicitation of individual prospects capable of giving in excess of $25,000. The Director of Development will be responsible for major gifts fundraising within the School of Law and UND, including arranging cultivation and solicitation visits with individuals, corporations, foundations and the development of proposals for private funding. This position is responsible for expanding the organization’s donor base by forging new relationships with potential donors of all levels. The Director of Development is responsible for building and maintaining a portfolio of 90-120 and major gift prospects and soliciting them for multi-year pledges. The Director of Development will actively engage the prospects in the portfolio and schedule approximately 100-125 personal visits annually.
ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS
FUNDRAISING
Work with the Vice President of Development and the School of Law department to create and implement a development plan for the School of Law.
Work in conjunction with the Vice President of Development and the Dean to establish performance goals in assigned areas, monitor progress against goals and devise strategies to ensure success in meeting these goals.
Qualify, cultivate, solicit and close major and planned gifts from individuals, corporations, foundations, and friends to reach predetermined goal while maintaining and growing existing relationships to benefit UND.

new_jobs.title: Associate Director of Development (Development Officer), Eskenazi Museum of Art
new_jobs.description:
ART MUSEUM (BL-AMUS-IUBLA)

Since its establishment in 1941, the Sidney and Lois Eskenazi Museum of Art at Indiana University (IU) has grown from a small university teaching collection into one of the foremost university art museums in the country. A preeminent teaching museum, its internationally acclaimed collection includes more than 48,000 objects representing nearly every art-producing culture throughout history. Collection areas include African art, ancient art, Asian art, global contemporary art, European and American Art, Indigenous art, Oceanic art, and prints, drawings, and photography.

The Associate Director of Development designs and implements engagement and solicitation strategies for the Eskenazi Museum of Art¿s donors, and prospective donors.

Department Specific Responsibilities

Plays a critical role in the museum's annual fundraising and stewardship strategies, particularly when it comes to cultivating early-stage donors and donor prospects.
Supervises development staff and sets priorities for the museum's development activities in consultation and collaboration with the museum's Senior Director of Development.
Responsibilities include stewardship, soliciting annual support (restricted and unrestricted), supervising development staff, event planning and implementation, establishing or expanding relationships with donors, and coordinating with key partners across the museum and university.
Responsible for ensuring that practices follow Eskenazi Museum of Art and IU Foundation objectives and policies, and for developing and tracking the development department budget as part of the planning process.
Cultivates donor relationships through segmented stewardship and solicitation messaging, regular communication and outreach, including thank you messages and consistent updates on the impact of philanthropic support.
Maintains the Crimson database and Workfront or AlumniQ list pulls and solicitation approvals, and forwards prospective and current donor information to the Senior Director of Development and museum director.
With Senior Director of Development and museum director, sets annual giving targets, contacts, and timelines by campaign. Tracks progress toward goals, reporting and presenting figures to museum leadership.
Elevates the museum¿s overall advancement strategy.
Maintains a portfolio of 50-75 mid-level prospects. Creates proposals, solicits and closes gifts from $1,000 up to $49,999 with an emphasis on annual giving and encourages multi-year commitments regularly.
Oversees annual fund.
Strategically identifies and develops engagement strategies that provide opportunities for donors to be meaningfully involved in the museum¿s mission and programs designed to catalyze personal connections with museum programs and staff.
Oversees the design and production of donor-related marketing and communication, including online, social media and web content.
Collaborates with the Senior Director of Development, museum director, development and museum staff to facilitate programming and communication for the museum¿s National Advisory Board organization, communication, travel, and activities.
Fosters collaborative relationships with museum staff and university advancement partners to expand and diversify the donor network, and advocates for the museum.
Develops and implements (with the support of the Development Coordinator) events that engage museum supporters who have the capacity to make early stage and major gifts. Events may include donor receptions in major markets, on-campus guest speakers, museum tours and art viewing opportunities, and lunch and learns.
Uses advancement data to ensure strategic allocation of resources when planning and implementing events and sends follow-up messaging and associated metrics after events.
Researches, compiles, and provides metrics, facts, and general operations information to donors.
Regularly collaborates with museum colleagues to answer donor queries related to their interest in giving/contributing.
Provides list of major gift prospects to Senior Director of Development and museum director and develops opportunities to engage them with the museum.
Provides day-to-day operational management of development office, including staff and intern responsibilities, if needed. Sets goals and analyzes, monitors, and evaluates performance of assigned staff. Train and manage interns.

General Responsibilities

Initiates and assumes responsibility for the identification, cultivation, solicitation and stewardship of a portfolio and/or a region of prospects and donors.
Plays a major role in the planning, implementation and coordination of fundraising activities by coordinating and driving specific engagement strategies.
Serves as the unit liaison among internal and external stakeholder groups, cultivating relationships, and providing organizational information and representing the interests of the unit.
Advances knowledge of the university's missions, goals of the individual unit and development program objectives.
Facilitates productive relationships daily between donors and top IU administrators, faculty and staff to ensure effectiveness of donor strategy plans to meet their individual goals.
May provide guidance to other staff engaged in fundraising/development activities.

Combinations of related education and experience may be considered. Education beyond the minimum required may be substituted for work experience. Work experience beyond the minimum required may be substituted for education.

EDUCATION

Required

Bachelor's degree in related field.

Required

WORK EXPERIENCE

5 years of experience in fundraising/development, sales, communications, public relations, a higher education foundation, or related field.

Preferred

Project management experience, coordinating initiatives involving multiple collaborators and stakeholders, and organizational leadership

Proficient written and verbal communication skills.
Maintains a high degree of professionalism.
Ability to build strong customer relationships.

Demonstrates a high commitment to quality.
